## Agent API Overview

The Agent API is specifically for access by third party agents who will be buying tickets from the system owner through a credit agreement.

## Integration Terms

The system owner will provide access credentials for agents, who can each be set up with multiple customer records, each with different sales commission agreements, seat access and discounting where necessary.

Agents will need a separate e-mail address for each record held on a single system, and will be asked to provide a mobile phone number for 2 factor authentication purposes.

## Ticket Sales and Operations

Using the API, Agents can sell directly from your live allocation by replicating your Seating Plan and hosting this on their website, which means that real time changes made to Events and Seating Plans on your system will be reflected on their website.

The Agent mode allows the creation, management and confirmation of multiple concurrent baskets, and provides full end-to-end purchase, with all transactions recorded against system credit logged against the specific API user's account.

Agents only have access to sell tickets via the API.

For more detailed technical documentation, you can refer to the Spektrix Integrate Portal and their support resources.

Using the API, Agents can sell directly from your live allocation by replicating your Seating Plan and hosting this on their website, which means that real time changes made to Events and Seating Plans on your system will be reflected on their website.

The Agent mode allows the creation, management and confirmation of multiple concurrent baskets, and provides full end-to-end purchase, with all transactions recorded against system credit logged against the specific API user's account.

Agents only have access to sell tickets via the API.

For more detailed technical documentation, you can refer to the Spektrix Integrate Portal and their support resources.

- A unique email address per agent customer record
- A mobile phone number for two-factor authentication

There are no described costs or formal approval procedures beyond the client's internal setup process.

findings.fact: PBH's Free Fringe model: no venue hire charge, free entrance for everyone, and audiences put a voluntary donation in a bucket at the end; it publishes its own printed programme, the Wee Blue Book, and claims 'over 600 shows and 10,000 performances in 2018'.

PBH's ethos/conditions forbid charging admission ('The shows are free to the public to attend'); performers make a 'bucket speech' for donations, and applicants must not also have a free-admission show with any other organisation (explicitly naming Laughing Horse).

Fringe Society registration is optional for PBH Free Fringe performers — the performers' FAQ states 'It's not compulsory to be in the program and it isn't cheap' — so PBH shows can exist only in PBH's own listings/Wee Blue Book and never appear on edfringe.com.

PBH's own site lists its 2026 programme (8-30 Aug 2026) across 50+ venue spaces with filters by genre/venue/time/date, paginated over 34 pages at ~24 entries per full page (~795 listing entries), versus only 183 PBH shows in the edfringe 2026 catalogue — implying most PBH shows are not Fringe-registered.

Laughing Horse's Free Festival (freefestival.co.uk, run by Laughing Horse Festivals Ltd) is free entry with a collection on the way out; some shows offer 'Pay What You Can' advance tickets which go '100% to the performer' and are booked via the Fringe Box Office up to 30 minutes before a show — not Eventbrite or their own checkout. Average donations: £2-3 unticketed, £6-8 PWYC.

The Free Festival usually has over 20 venues and more than 40 performance spaces and lists all its shows on its own site freefestival.co.uk with date/genre/venue/time filtering; the model is 'moving the busking indoors'.

In EdFringeNow's own edfringe scrape of the 2026 catalogue (data as of 2026-07-28): 27 'PBH's Free Fringe @ …' and 18 'Laughing Horse @ …' venue records exist; all 183 PBH shows have FREE_NON_TICKETED performances (zero FREE_TICKETED, consistent with PBH's no-tickets-ever ethos); Laughing Horse's 320 shows split 103 FREE_NON_TICKETED / 215 TICKETS_AVAILABLE (the PWYC shows sold as ordinary Fringe Box Office tickets).

Free shows appear in edfringe data like any other show: the API's ticketStatusOptions enum includes FREE_NON_TICKETED and FREE_TICKETED, and in the 2026 scrape 422 of 4,100 shows carry a FREE_* status (399 FREE_NON_TICKETED, 23 FREE_TICKETED); FREE_TICKETED (free but reserve a ticket) is used only by non-PBH/non-Laughing-Horse venues such as Fringe Central events.

Paradise Green is a volunteer-run, not-for-profit organisation running Fringe venues each summer: Paradise in Augustines (Sanctuary 110 seats, Studio 107, The Snug 30) and Paradise in the Vault; both venues are in the edfringe 2026 catalogue.

Bedlam Theatre (Venue 49), a ~90-seat converted neo-gothic church, is the year-round home of the Edinburgh University Theatre Company and runs its own Fringe programme (Bedlam Fringe, bedlamfringe.co.uk) — active for 2025 (Bedlam Late lineup coverage) and present in the 2026 catalogue.

Hill Street Theatre (Venue 41, 19 Hill St) — a Fringe mainstay previously run under Edinburgh Little Theatre, Assembly, Universal Arts and C primo banners — operated as 'Braw Venues @ Hill Street' for 2025, and both 'Braw Venues @ Hill Street' and 'Braw Venues @ Grand Lodge' appear in the 2026 catalogue.

The Quaker Meeting House (7 Victoria Terrace, historic Venue 40) is programmed during the Fringe by C ARTS as 'C alto'; the 2026 edfringe venue record id 40 is named 'C ARTS | C venues | C alto' with address 'Quaker Meeting House, 7 Victoria Terrace'.

The Institut français d'Écosse runs its curated 'Vive le Fringe!' festival (1-25 Aug 2025) at its premises at the top of the Royal Mile, with French and Scottish artists; it appears in the 2026 edfringe catalogue as 'French Institute in Scotland'.

Riddle's Court on the Royal Mile is operated at the Fringe by Greenside ('Greenside @ Riddles Court', since Fringe 2022; previously PQA Venues) and is in the 2026 catalogue alongside Greenside @ George Street.

Sweet Venues no longer operates in Edinburgh: its site lists only Brighton (Sweet@The Yellow Book) and Dundee (Sweet@The Steps Theatre) operations, with no Edinburgh Fringe presence, and no Sweet venue appears in the 2026 edfringe catalogue.

Army @ The Fringe (Hepburn House, 89 East Claremont St, in association with Summerhall, running since 2017) has an edfringe venue page and its own site, but armyatthefringe.org returned 503, the Scotsman 'revival' coverage dates to 2021, and no Army @ The Fringe venue or show appears in the 2026 catalogue — 2025/2026 activity unconfirmed.

The Fringe is open-access ('unjuried'): 'there is no selection committee, and anyone may participate', but 'participating in the Fringe requires registration, payment of a registration fee, and use of a Fringe venue'; the Fringe Society 'publishes the programme, sells tickets to all events from a central physical box office and website'. 2025 scale: 3,893 shows, 53,942 performances, 301 venues, 2.6m+ tickets.

Show registration with the Fringe Society is done via edfringe.com/edfringeware with a registration fee (from £96 incl VAT for a 1-2 performance run per search snippets of the official registration pages, which block direct fetching).

Venue registration with the Fringe Society is free of charge; registered venues and spaces appear on 'the online interactive map that lists all venues (tickets.edfringe.com/venues)' and printed in the back of the Fringe programme — i.e., the Fringe Society publishes an enumerable venue directory. Ticketed shows must allocate a minimum of 25% of tickets to the Fringe Box Office.

The edfringe GraphQL API exposes this venue directory directly (VenueTypeAhead query): EdFringeNow's venues.json holds 301 venue records with name/address/postcode/lat/lng for 2026 — a machine-readable enumeration of every registered provider location.

An 'Association of Independent Venue Producers' exists at fringealliance.org (search metadata claims it represents independent venue producers accounting for 85% of Fringe tickets sold and that it co-developed a Best Practice Code for Fringe Venues with the Fringe Society), but the site itself is a dormant template with unfilled {{Name}}/{{URL}} placeholders and a 2007-2023 copyright — not a usable enumeration source.

keyClaims: The official edfringe catalogue is the exhaustive universe of REGISTERED shows and venues (open-access festival, but paid show registration + free venue registration with the Fringe Society are what put you 'in the Fringe'), and the venue directory is enumerable both on tickets.edfringe.com/venues and via the API's VenueTypeAhead (301 records for 2026) — no active venue association offers a better list.

There is one demonstrable gap in that universe: Fringe Society registration is optional for PBH Free Fringe acts ('It's not compulsory to be in the program'), and PBH's own 2026 site lists ~795 entries across 50+ spaces versus only 183 PBH shows in the edfringe catalogue — so a large slice of the unticketed free programme lives only on freefringe.org.uk / the Wee Blue Book.

Free shows that ARE registered appear in edfringe data like any other show — FREE_NON_TICKETED (all 183 PBH shows), FREE_TICKETED (23 shows, non-PBH/LH), and Laughing Horse PWYC shows as ordinary TICKETS_AVAILABLE tickets sold through the Fringe Box Office — so the existing scrape already covers everything sellable, and the free-show operators present zero third-party ticket-selling opportunity (PBH has nothing to sell; Laughing Horse PWYC routes through the official box office).
openQuestions: Whether Army @ The Fringe ran in 2025 or is running in 2026 — its site was unreachable (503), recent press coverage dates to 2021, and it is absent from the 2026 edfringe catalogue.

The exact PBH 2026 show count and the true size of the unregistered-show gap: the ~795 figure is page-count arithmetic (34 pages x ~24 cards) and entries may include virtual shows or not map 1:1 to unique in-person shows; a direct crawl of freefringe.org.uk would settle it.
Whether the Association of Independent Venue Producers still operates in 2025/2026 (its website is a dormant template) and whether any current membership list exists anywhere.
Whether Laughing Horse ever uses non-edfringe ticketing (e.g. Eventbrite) for one-off events — none found, but not exhaustively ruled out.
Whether the C ARTS 'C alto' = Quaker Meeting House arrangement is confirmed by C ARTS' own 2026 materials (inferred from the edfringe venue record's address plus a third-party listing).
What exactly the edfringe.com 'Fringe venues' page (edfringe.com/experience/plan-your-visit/fringe-venues/) publishes beyond the interactive map, since edfringe.com blocks direct fetching (403).

Free shows do appear in edfringe data like any other show: the scrape's ticketStatus enum includes FREE_NON_TICKETED (399 shows) and FREE_TICKETED (23 shows), and every PBH-registered show carries FREE_NON_TICKETED — meaning the current scrape already covers the entire sellable and registered-free universe, and no free-show operator offers any third-party ticket-selling opportunity.

findings.fact: PBH's Free Fringe model: no venue hire charge, free entrance for everyone, and audiences put a voluntary donation in a bucket at the end; it publishes its own printed programme, the Wee Blue Book, and claims 'over 600 shows and 10,000 performances in 2018'.

PBH's ethos/conditions forbid charging admission ('The shows are free to the public to attend'); performers make a 'bucket speech' for donations, and applicants must not also have a free-admission show with any other organisation (explicitly naming Laughing Horse).

Fringe Society registration is optional for PBH Free Fringe performers — the performers' FAQ states 'It's not compulsory to be in the program and it isn't cheap' — so PBH shows can exist only in PBH's own listings/Wee Blue Book and never appear on edfringe.com.

PBH's own site lists its 2026 programme (8-30 Aug 2026) across 50+ venue spaces with filters by genre/venue/time/date, paginated over 34 pages at ~24 entries per full page (~795 listing entries), versus only 183 PBH shows in the edfringe 2026 catalogue — implying most PBH shows are not Fringe-registered.

Laughing Horse's Free Festival (freefestival.co.uk, run by Laughing Horse Festivals Ltd) is free entry with a collection on the way out; some shows offer 'Pay What You Can' advance tickets which go '100% to the performer' and are booked via the Fringe Box Office up to 30 minutes before a show — not Eventbrite or their own checkout. Average donations: £2-3 unticketed, £6-8 PWYC.

The Free Festival usually has over 20 venues and more than 40 performance spaces and lists all its shows on its own site freefestival.co.uk with date/genre/venue/time filtering; the model is 'moving the busking indoors'.

In EdFringeNow's own edfringe scrape of the 2026 catalogue (data as of 2026-07-28): 27 'PBH's Free Fringe @ …' and 18 'Laughing Horse @ …' venue records exist; all 183 PBH shows have FREE_NON_TICKETED performances (zero FREE_TICKETED, consistent with PBH's no-tickets-ever ethos); Laughing Horse's 320 shows split 103 FREE_NON_TICKETED / 215 TICKETS_AVAILABLE (the PWYC shows sold as ordinary Fringe Box Office tickets).

Free shows appear in edfringe data like any other show: the API's ticketStatusOptions enum includes FREE_NON_TICKETED and FREE_TICKETED, and in the 2026 scrape 422 of 4,100 shows carry a FREE_* status (399 FREE_NON_TICKETED, 23 FREE_TICKETED); FREE_TICKETED (free but reserve a ticket) is used only by non-PBH/non-Laughing-Horse venues such as Fringe Central events.

Paradise Green is a volunteer-run, not-for-profit organisation running Fringe venues each summer: Paradise in Augustines (Sanctuary 110 seats, Studio 107, The Snug 30) and Paradise in the Vault; both venues are in the edfringe 2026 catalogue.

Bedlam Theatre (Venue 49), a ~90-seat converted neo-gothic church, is the year-round home of the Edinburgh University Theatre Company and runs its own Fringe programme (Bedlam Fringe, bedlamfringe.co.uk) — active for 2025 (Bedlam Late lineup coverage) and present in the 2026 catalogue.

Hill Street Theatre (Venue 41, 19 Hill St) — a Fringe mainstay previously run under Edinburgh Little Theatre, Assembly, Universal Arts and C primo banners — operated as 'Braw Venues @ Hill Street' for 2025, and both 'Braw Venues @ Hill Street' and 'Braw Venues @ Grand Lodge' appear in the 2026 catalogue.

The Quaker Meeting House (7 Victoria Terrace, historic Venue 40) is programmed during the Fringe by C ARTS as 'C alto'; the 2026 edfringe venue record id 40 is named 'C ARTS | C venues | C alto' with address 'Quaker Meeting House, 7 Victoria Terrace'.

The Institut français d'Écosse runs its curated 'Vive le Fringe!' festival (1-25 Aug 2025) at its premises at the top of the Royal Mile, with French and Scottish artists; it appears in the 2026 edfringe catalogue as 'French Institute in Scotland'.

Riddle's Court on the Royal Mile is operated at the Fringe by Greenside ('Greenside @ Riddles Court', since Fringe 2022; previously PQA Venues) and is in the 2026 catalogue alongside Greenside @ George Street.

Sweet Venues no longer operates in Edinburgh: its site lists only Brighton (Sweet@The Yellow Book) and Dundee (Sweet@The Steps Theatre) operations, with no Edinburgh Fringe presence, and no Sweet venue appears in the 2026 edfringe catalogue.

Army @ The Fringe (Hepburn House, 89 East Claremont St, in association with Summerhall, running since 2017) has an edfringe venue page and its own site, but armyatthefringe.org returned 503, the Scotsman 'revival' coverage dates to 2021, and no Army @ The Fringe venue or show appears in the 2026 catalogue — 2025/2026 activity unconfirmed.

The Fringe is open-access ('unjuried'): 'there is no selection committee, and anyone may participate', but 'participating in the Fringe requires registration, payment of a registration fee, and use of a Fringe venue'; the Fringe Society 'publishes the programme, sells tickets to all events from a central physical box office and website'. 2025 scale: 3,893 shows, 53,942 performances, 301 venues, 2.6m+ tickets.

Show registration with the Fringe Society is done via edfringe.com/edfringeware with a registration fee (from £96 incl VAT for a 1-2 performance run per search snippets of the official registration pages, which block direct fetching).

Venue registration with the Fringe Society is free of charge; registered venues and spaces appear on 'the online interactive map that lists all venues (tickets.edfringe.com/venues)' and printed in the back of the Fringe programme — i.e., the Fringe Society publishes an enumerable venue directory. Ticketed shows must allocate a minimum of 25% of tickets to the Fringe Box Office.

The edfringe GraphQL API exposes this venue directory directly (VenueTypeAhead query): EdFringeNow's venues.json holds 301 venue records with name/address/postcode/lat/lng for 2026 — a machine-readable enumeration of every registered provider location.

An 'Association of Independent Venue Producers' exists at fringealliance.org (search metadata claims it represents independent venue producers accounting for 85% of Fringe tickets sold and that it co-developed a Best Practice Code for Fringe Venues with the Fringe Society), but the site itself is a dormant template with unfilled {{Name}}/{{URL}} placeholders and a 2007-2023 copyright — not a usable enumeration source.

keyClaims: The official edfringe catalogue is the exhaustive universe of REGISTERED shows and venues (open-access festival, but paid show registration + free venue registration with the Fringe Society are what put you 'in the Fringe'), and the venue directory is enumerable both on tickets.edfringe.com/venues and via the API's VenueTypeAhead (301 records for 2026) — no active venue association offers a better list.

There is one demonstrable gap in that universe: Fringe Society registration is optional for PBH Free Fringe acts ('It's not compulsory to be in the program'), and PBH's own 2026 site lists ~795 entries across 50+ spaces versus only 183 PBH shows in the edfringe catalogue — so a large slice of the unticketed free programme lives only on freefringe.org.uk / the Wee Blue Book.

Free shows that ARE registered appear in edfringe data like any other show — FREE_NON_TICKETED (all 183 PBH shows), FREE_TICKETED (23 shows, non-PBH/LH), and Laughing Horse PWYC shows as ordinary TICKETS_AVAILABLE tickets sold through the Fringe Box Office — so the existing scrape already covers everything sellable, and the free-show operators present zero third-party ticket-selling opportunity (PBH has nothing to sell; Laughing Horse PWYC routes through the official box office).
openQuestions: Whether Army @ The Fringe ran in 2025 or is running in 2026 — its site was unreachable (503), recent press coverage dates to 2021, and it is absent from the 2026 edfringe catalogue.

The exact PBH 2026 show count and the true size of the unregistered-show gap: the ~795 figure is page-count arithmetic (34 pages x ~24 cards) and entries may include virtual shows or not map 1:1 to unique in-person shows; a direct crawl of freefringe.org.uk would settle it.
Whether the Association of Independent Venue Producers still operates in 2025/2026 (its website is a dormant template) and whether any current membership list exists anywhere.
Whether Laughing Horse ever uses non-edfringe ticketing (e.g. Eventbrite) for one-off events — none found, but not exhaustively ruled out.
Whether the C ARTS 'C alto' = Quaker Meeting House arrangement is confirmed by C ARTS' own 2026 materials (inferred from the edfringe venue record's address plus a third-party listing).
What exactly the edfringe.com 'Fringe venues' page (edfringe.com/experience/plan-your-visit/fringe-venues/) publishes beyond the interactive map, since edfringe.com blocks direct fetching (403).

CONTEXT (shared by all researchers):
You are researching for EdFringeNow, a client-side web product for the Edinburgh Festival Fringe (discovery + trip planner). The repo currently gets its show catalogue by scraping edfringe.com's GraphQL API (Tikketr platform, edfringe-tikketr-web-api.equhost.com) nightly via GitHub Actions. The owner wants to understand how Fringe tickets are ACTUALLY sold, who all the "event providers" (venue operators) are, whether a third party can sell tickets itself (affiliate/agent/API), and whether provider or aggregator listings APIs could replace the edfringe scrape.

TODAY is 2026-07-31. The 2026 Fringe runs 7-31 August (3,649 shows, 258 venues). Prefer 2025/2026 sources; older sources are fine for structural facts if you say so.

TOOLING CONSTRAINTS: You have WebSearch and WebFetch. edfringe.com returns 403 to WebFetch and equhost.com is blocked by the egress proxy - for those domains rely on WebSearch result snippets and third-party coverage. Most other sites (venue operators, news, wikis) are fetchable; if a fetch fails, fall back to search. Cite EVERY fact with a real URL you actually saw.

OUTPUT: your final output is consumed by a script, not a human. Fill the schema honestly: mark confidence low when a claim rests on one thin source; put what you could NOT establish into openQuestions rather than guessing. keyClaims = the 2-3 claims your topic's conclusions rest on (the ones that, if wrong, change the product decision).

TOPIC: Listings DATA sources - could anything replace scraping edfringe.com?

We already know (from prior repo research): the official Edinburgh Festivals Listings API (api.edinburghfestivalcity.com, run by Festivals Edinburgh) is free with a registered key, covers all major festivals including the Fringe, exposes performances with start/end/price and venue lat/long, BUT has no per-performance availability/sold-out field, requires attribution, forbids redistributing dumps to third parties, and requires refreshing at least every 24h. Do NOT re-research those basics; go BEYOND them:
1. The Fringe-specific angle of that API: is its Fringe feed the same data as edfringe.com (it is the official listings database - who feeds it, how fresh is it during August, does it include Free Fringe / Free Festival shows)? Any published note on its Fringe update cadence or completeness vs edfringe.com?
2. Do any VENUE OPERATORS publish machine-readable listings: JSON endpoints, public APIs, iCal feeds on assemblyfestival.com, pleasance.co.uk, underbellyedinburgh.co.uk, gildedballoon.co.uk, summerhall, monkeybarrelcomedy.com, thestand.co.uk? Probe lightly with WebFetch where fetchable (e.g. look for /api/, wp-json, .json script tags mentioned in page source descriptions) and search for developer docs. Report honestly if nothing public exists.
3. Aggregators: Data Thistle events API (commercial - pricing/terms if findable), The List, Skiddle, Ents24, WeGotTickets, Eventbrite - do any carry substantial Fringe listings with an API?
4. Bottom line: for a product needing ALL ~3,650 shows with per-performance times AND ticket-availability status, rank the options: keep scraping edfringe GraphQL / official Listings API / per-operator feeds / aggregators. Which combination is actually viable and what does each lack?

Festival listings data changes regularly throughout the year and in particular over the summer, and applications should retrieve fresh data from the API at least every 24 hours to ensure displaying accurate information.

# Edinburgh Festivals Events API Fields

## Core Event Fields
The API returns an "id" (unique identifier), "title", "description", "artist", and "status" indicating whether an event is active, cancelled, or deleted.

## Performance Details
Each event contains a "performances" array with:
- "start" and "end" times
- "price" and "concession" pricing
- "price_string" for display
- "duration_minutes"
- "is_at_fixed_time" (boolean for drop-in events)

## Availability & Status
The API does not explicitly return a "sold_out" field. However, "status" values indicate: empty/missing/active (display normally), "cancelled" (event cancelled), or "deleted" (must remove from local database).

## Festival Values
The "festival_id" field accepts these values: "fringe, demofringe, jazz, book, international, tattoo, art, hogmanay, science, imaginate, film, mela, storytelling."

## Timestamps & Data Freshness
- "updated" indicates when the event record changed
- "modified_from" query parameter enables synchronization, with the note that there may be "a delay of a few minutes between an event being marked as modified and it being returned in an API query"
- Documentation recommends adding a ten-minute window to catch all changes during sync operations

## Additional Details
Accessibility fields include "has_audio_description", "has_captioning", "has_signed", and "has_other_accessibility" with corresponding date arrays.

## Ticket Allocation

Every ticketed show must allocate a minimum of 25% of its tickets per performance to the Fringe Box Office. The Fringe Box Office is allocated a percentage of tickets to sell on behalf of each show – this varies between shows and venues.

## Venue and Fringe Box Office Options

If your venue does not run a ticketing facility, you are welcome to allocate all of your tickets for sale through the Fringe Box Office. Venues can also allocate additional tickets to the Fringe Box Office at any time.

## Commission and Payout

A 5% (plus VAT) commission from the sale of every ticket sold through the Fringe Box Office is payable to The Edinburgh Festival Fringe Society. ## Ticket Sales Volume

The Fringe Box Office sold over 2.6 million tickets in 2025.

findings.fact: The Fringe Society publishes no affiliate scheme, ticket-agent programme, white-label box office, or public purchase API; repeated targeted searches of edfringe.com participant/artist services, box office, and registration help pages surface only the Fringe Box Office (central agency), Fringe Friends (consumer membership), and the approval-gated listings API.

Every ticketed Fringe show must allocate a minimum of 25% of tickets per performance to the Fringe Box Office; the Fringe Society charges 'a 5% (plus VAT) commission from the sale of every ticket sold through the Fringe Box Office', with payout by end of September — i.e. the Society itself operates as an agent selling on behalf of shows.

Fringe Society ticketing terms state purchasers 'agree not to use tickets for any commercial, business or re-sale purposes' — an explicit bar on unauthorized commercial resale of Fringe Box Office tickets.

The official third-party data route is the Edinburgh Festivals Listings API (Festivals Edinburgh Ltd, built by inGenerator): free, commercial use permitted, but Fringe access is approval-gated (dummy 'demofringe' data until approved) and it is listings-only — no purchase capability.

The Listings API licence forbids affiliate-style routing for Fringe shows: 'Links relating to Fringe shows or events must not be made to any other ticketing site, including the venue's own site' — links must go to edfringe.com — and redistribution of the data as feeds/dumps is prohibited; the licence is revocable at will.

The Listings API status page shows Edinburgh Festival Fringe data available for 2012-2025 and 2026 (subject to approval), so it remains a live, licensed alternative to scraping edfringe.com's GraphQL for the catalogue itself.

Gilded Balloon's 2026 ticket T&Cs state 'All Gilded Balloon tickets are sold through the Red61 VIA ticketing platform on behalf of the artists', with a £1.25/ticket booking fee on Fringe shows (max £6.25/transaction); its resale clause only prohibits resale 'if prohibited by law'; no agent or affiliate programme is mentioned and the website may be used for browsing and booking 'and for no other purposes'.

No affiliate or agent programme is advertised by Assembly, Pleasance, Underbelly, Gilded Balloon, Summerhall, Monkey Barrel, or The Stand; searches for such programmes return only their consumer offers and the EdFest joint venture.

EdFest.com is the venues' own closed aggregator: 'a unique collaboration' of Assembly, C ARTS, Gilded Balloon, Just the Tonic, Pleasance, Underbelly and ZOO, selling cross-venue tickets in a single basket; for 2026 it advertises zero-commission ticketing across ~1,273 productions, a £5 cap on booking fees, and the Love the Fringe paid membership (tiers ~£30-£450, revenue split 50/50 with venues).

EdFest/Love the Fringe runs on Red61 infrastructure — participating artists 'manage their Love the Fringe ticket allocation directly through their Red61 reporting site' — i.e. the cross-venue selling network is a Red61 VIA capability shared among the JV operators, not open to outsiders.

Red61 VIA offers an API ('build your own custom ticketing journey'), a hosted white-label web sales solution, and 'collaborative cross-selling with partner venues and events', and says VIA was 'built to sustain the high ticket volumes and cross-selling functionality of the world's biggest arts festival, the Edinburgh Festival Fringe' — but access is by commercial engagement (request a demo/contract), with no self-service or published pricing.

Red61 'ran the Fringe Society box office from 2009 to 2023' and still processes the Fringe's largest venue network (360 venues, 600+ spaces, ~55,000 performances; clients include ZOO and the Famous Spiegeltent), with systems that 'enabled clients to cross-sell and collaborate with venue and sales partners' (article dated 18 Aug 2025).

Spektrix operates a dedicated Agency API 'for access by third party agents who will be buying tickets from the system owner through a credit agreement': the venue creates the agent's record, sets commission, seat access and allocations per agreement, and the API supports full end-to-end purchase (excluding payment processing) — proving third-party agent selling is technically supported but requires a per-venue commercial agreement, set up by the venue.

Spektrix support docs confirm 'The Agent API is specifically for access by third party agents who will be buying tickets from the system owner through a credit agreement' and that agents can replicate live seating plans and allocations on their own website.

The Fringe Society's current box office platform is Tikketr, built by equ (Equilibrium Interactive) — the official EdFringe app package is com.tikketr.edfringe.prod — and no public partner, agent, or purchase API for Tikketr/equ could be found anywhere.

Ticketsolve's XML API exists 'to allow 3rd party web applications to pull event information from the Ticketsolve system into the clients CMS' — a venue-side website integration, not an open agent/reseller channel; TicketCo likewise exposes organiser-level API docs (apidoc.ticketco.events) rather than an open reseller programme.
Citizen Ticket (Edinburgh-based platform) offers organisers embeddable ticket widgets for their own sites and payment integrations, but no public third-party agent/affiliate API was found.

TodayTix carries no current Edinburgh Fringe (Edinburgh, August) inventory — its Fringe-related listings are London/NYC transfers and previews of shows with Fringe heritage (e.g. Kathy and Stella Solve a Murder!, Fringe-preview workshop shows).

Fever does not sell Edinburgh Fringe tickets: its 'Edinburgh Festival Fringe Society' venue page is an empty placeholder ('Experiences... are coming soon') with no partnership evidence; its Fringe-branded inventory is London 'Edinburgh Fringe Preview' events where Fever is the promoter's primary ticketer, not a Fringe reseller.

Third parties do distribute Fringe-adjacent products under explicit deals: LivingSocial retails 'Love The Fringe Membership: Six Festival Tickets & Exclusive Offers' as a voucher deal — memberships/offers, not direct ticket inventory.

The Stand Comedy Club's Edinburgh events are retailed by mainstream agents See Tickets and Ents24 (Ents24 'books official tickets'), showing venue-by-venue agency deals do happen — but this covers the club's own programme and there is no sign these agents carry the venue's August Fringe runs or that other Fringe operators use them.
Monkey Barrel Comedy sells its Fringe tickets through its own site (calendar/checkout links via tockify.com/monkey.barrel) and the Fringe Box Office, with no affiliate or partner channel mentioned.
The Fringe Society does run a 'Fringe Friends' consumer membership (2for1 tickets; Society retains 65% of net Friends income), but this is a fan membership, not a trade/affiliate channel.

keyClaims: Neither the Edinburgh Festival Fringe Society nor any major venue operator offers an open affiliate, agent, white-label, or public purchase API; the only sanctioned data channel (Edinburgh Festivals Listings API) is listings-only and its licence forbids linking Fringe shows to any ticketing site other than edfringe.com.

Third-party selling of Fringe inventory is technically possible only through per-operator commercial agreements on the operators' own platforms (e.g. Spektrix's Agency API via a credit agreement the venue sets up; Red61 VIA API/white-label under contract) — there is no self-service route, no published commission rates, and the Fringe Society's own platform (Tikketr/equ) exposes no partner API at all.

The large venue operators have channelled cross-venue selling into their own closed joint venture EdFest.com (Red61-based, 7 operators, zero-commission/Love the Fringe model), and Fringe Society ticket T&Cs prohibit using tickets for 'commercial, business or re-sale purposes' — so for a small independent site the realistic option is uncommissioned deep links to edfringe.com and venue box offices, not selling.
openQuestions: Exact full text of edfringe.com's website/ticketing T&Cs (site returns 403 to fetching): the precise resale clause wording and whether scraping/automated access of edfringe.com is explicitly prohibited — only a search-snippet of the 'commercial, business or re-sale purposes' clause was verifiable.

Whether any Fringe venue operator would actually grant an agent/credit agreement to a small independent site, and at what commission — no operator publishes agent terms or rates; this can only be established by contacting Assembly/Pleasance/Underbelly/etc. or Red61 directly.

Which ticketing platform each big operator uses in 2026 beyond those confirmed (Gilded Balloon = Red61 VIA per its T&Cs; EdFest JV = Red61; Fringe Society = Tikketr/equ): Assembly, Pleasance, Underbelly and Summerhall's current platforms were not independently pinned down, and no Fringe venue was confirmed to run Spektrix.

Whether the Edinburgh Festivals Listings API currently has 2026 Fringe data populated and what the Fringe-approval turnaround/criteria are in practice (status page lists 2026 availability but not row counts).

Whether See Tickets/Ents24 carry The Stand's August Fringe performances or only its year-round club shows, and whether any hotel-concierge or tourism-trade channel holds a formal Fringe ticket agency (no evidence found either way).
Whether Tikketr/equ (Equilibrium Interactive) offers any non-public partner or agent integration to venues or agents on request — nothing public exists, but a private capability cannot be ruled out.

Monkey Barrel Comedy sells its Fringe tickets through its own site (calendar/checkout links via tockify.com/monkey.barrel) and the Fringe Box Office, with no affiliate or partner channel mentioned.
The Fringe Society does run a 'Fringe Friends' consumer membership (2for1 tickets; Society retains 65% of net Friends income), but this is a fan membership, not a trade/affiliate channel.

keyClaims: Neither the Edinburgh Festival Fringe Society nor any major venue operator offers an open affiliate, agent, white-label, or public purchase API; the only sanctioned data channel (Edinburgh Festivals Listings API) is listings-only and its licence forbids linking Fringe shows to any ticketing site other than edfringe.com.

Third-party selling of Fringe inventory is technically possible only through per-operator commercial agreements on the operators' own platforms (e.g. Spektrix's Agency API via a credit agreement the venue sets up; Red61 VIA API/white-label under contract) — there is no self-service route, no published commission rates, and the Fringe Society's own platform (Tikketr/equ) exposes no partner API at all.

The large venue operators have channelled cross-venue selling into their own closed joint venture EdFest.com (Red61-based, 7 operators, zero-commission/Love the Fringe model), and Fringe Society ticket T&Cs prohibit using tickets for 'commercial, business or re-sale purposes' — so for a small independent site the realistic option is uncommissioned deep links to edfringe.com and venue box offices, not selling.
openQuestions: Exact full text of edfringe.com's website/ticketing T&Cs (site returns 403 to fetching): the precise resale clause wording and whether scraping/automated access of edfringe.com is explicitly prohibited — only a search-snippet of the 'commercial, business or re-sale purposes' clause was verifiable.

Whether any Fringe venue operator would actually grant an agent/credit agreement to a small independent site, and at what commission — no operator publishes agent terms or rates; this can only be established by contacting Assembly/Pleasance/Underbelly/etc. or Red61 directly.

Which ticketing platform each big operator uses in 2026 beyond those confirmed (Gilded Balloon = Red61 VIA per its T&Cs; EdFest JV = Red61; Fringe Society = Tikketr/equ): Assembly, Pleasance, Underbelly and Summerhall's current platforms were not independently pinned down, and no Fringe venue was confirmed to run Spektrix.

Whether the Edinburgh Festivals Listings API currently has 2026 Fringe data populated and what the Fringe-approval turnaround/criteria are in practice (status page lists 2026 availability but not row counts).

Whether See Tickets/Ents24 carry The Stand's August Fringe performances or only its year-round club shows, and whether any hotel-concierge or tourism-trade channel holds a formal Fringe ticket agency (no evidence found either way).
Whether Tikketr/equ (Equilibrium Interactive) offers any non-public partner or agent integration to venues or agents on request — nothing public exists, but a private capability cannot be ruled out.

You are analyzing a local dataset - NO web access needed; do not use WebSearch/WebFetch.

Repo: /home/user/EdFringeNow. File: data/normalized/shows.json - a JSON array of ~4,100 Edinburgh Fringe 2026 shows. Relevant fields per show: "venue" (venue code string), "venueName" (e.g. "Dexter at Underbelly, Bristo Square"), "free" (boolean).

TASK: produce the definitive operator (venue-family) breakdown of the 2026 programme.
1. Write a python3 script in the scratchpad dir (do NOT modify or add any repo files; read-only on the repo).
2. Extract distinct venues: map venue code -> venueName (one name per code; if a code has several names, keep the most common).
3. Group venues into OPERATOR FAMILIES by matching venueName against operator patterns (case-insensitive substring), checking longer/more-specific patterns first. Seed patterns (extend if you notice more families in the data): Assembly; Pleasance; Underbelly; Gilded Balloon; Summerhall; ZOO; "C ARTS" / "C venues" / "C aquila" / "C alto" (venueName often starts "C " or contains "C ARTS"); theSpace; Greenside; Just the Tonic; Monkey Barrel; "The Stand"; Laughing Horse; PBH / "Free Fringe"; Sweet; Paradise; Traverse; Dance Base; Scottish Storytelling; Bedlam; Army @ The Fringe; French Institute / Institut; Quaker; Hill Street; Riddle's Court; St Andrew Square / other.
4. For each family: number of distinct venue codes, number of shows, up to 5 example venueNames. Sort by show count descending.
5. Everything unmatched goes in unmatchedVenues as "venueName (N shows)" sorted by show count descending - list ALL of them, do not truncate to a top-N; this tail is the point of the exercise.
6. Also report: total shows, total distinct venue codes, count of shows with free=true.
7. In "method", describe the matching approach and its caveats (e.g. venueName substring matching can mis-file a venue whose name merely mentions an operator; note any you spotted and hand-fixed).
Sanity checks: totals must add up (sum of family shows + unmatched shows = total shows). Iterate on the patterns until the unmatched tail is genuinely small independents rather than obvious families.

total = len(shows)

for s in shows:
    c = s['venue']
    names[c][s['venueName']] += 1
    code_shows[c] += 1
venue = {c: cnt.most_common(1)[0][0] for c, cnt in names.items()}

    'totalShows': total,
    'totalVenues': len(venue),
    'freeShows': free,
}
print(json.dumps(result, indent=1))

## Overview

Ents24 is a live entertainment website that provides listings, information, and directs visitors to tickets for events encompassing live music, clubbing, cinema, theatre, arts, days out and stand-up comedy. The site contains details of around 100,000 events happening across the UK at any given time.

## API Access

The Ents24 REST API gives you easy access to the UK's most comprehensive live entertainment database, with event-listing experts adding over 10,000 new listings every week. You can easily use the data for your website or application.

CONTEXT (shared by all researchers):
You are researching for EdFringeNow, a client-side web product for the Edinburgh Festival Fringe (discovery + trip planner). The repo currently gets its show catalogue by scraping edfringe.com's GraphQL API (Tikketr platform, edfringe-tikketr-web-api.equhost.com) nightly via GitHub Actions. The owner wants to understand how Fringe tickets are ACTUALLY sold, who all the "event providers" (venue operators) are, whether a third party can sell tickets itself (affiliate/agent/API), and whether provider or aggregator listings APIs could replace the edfringe scrape.

TODAY is 2026-07-31. The 2026 Fringe runs 7-31 August (3,649 shows, 258 venues). Prefer 2025/2026 sources; older sources are fine for structural facts if you say so.

TOOLING CONSTRAINTS: You have WebSearch and WebFetch. edfringe.com returns 403 to WebFetch and equhost.com is blocked by the egress proxy - for those domains rely on WebSearch result snippets and third-party coverage. Most other sites (venue operators, news, wikis) are fetchable; if a fetch fails, fall back to search. Cite EVERY fact with a real URL you actually saw.

OUTPUT: your final output is consumed by a script, not a human. Fill the schema honestly: mark confidence low when a claim rests on one thin source; put what you could NOT establish into openQuestions rather than guessing. keyClaims = the 2-3 claims your topic's conclusions rest on (the ones that, if wrong, change the product decision).

You are an ADVERSARIAL fact-checker. A researcher investigating "architecture" for the Edinburgh Fringe ticketing landscape rests their conclusions on the claims below. Your job is to try to REFUTE each claim with your own independent web searches - do not reuse the researcher's sources as confirmation; find your own. A claim is "confirmed" only if independent evidence supports it; "plausible" if consistent with what you found but not independently confirmed; "refuted" if you found contrary evidence (then write the correction); "unverifiable" if the public record genuinely doesn't settle it. Be especially suspicious of: ownership claims (who runs/owns a website), "no such scheme exists" negatives (search for the scheme yourself before agreeing), and platform/vendor claims (which ticketing tech powers which site).

CLAIMS:
1. edfringe.com is run by the Edinburgh Festival Fringe Society — an independent, membership-governed registered charity and company limited by guarantee that no venue operator owns or controls (they have publicly feuded with it) — and its box office sells each show under an allocation model (minimum 25% of tickets per performance, 5%+VAT commission), with NO_ALLOCATION_CONTACT_VENUE meaning the central allocation is exhausted but the venue's own Red61 box office may still have tickets.
2. edfest.com, by contrast, really is the major venue operators' own storefront: operated by Showcatcher Ltd (company 07628569, led by Assembly founder William Burdett-Coutts) as a declared ticket agent for seven operators (Assembly, C ARTS, Gilded Balloon, Just the Tonic, Pleasance, Underbelly, ZOO) on Red61 rails — so it covers only those venues' shows, never the full ~3,600-show catalogue.
3. Since March 2025 edfringe.com and the official app run on equ's Tikketr platform (the API the repo scrapes) as an explicitly interim system — Red61 ran the Society's ticketing until 2023/24 and still powers the venue operators' own box offices, and a permanent Storm ID-built site is due for Fringe 2027, meaning the scrape target is likely to change again and remains the only single source covering every registered show.

2. edfest.com, by contrast, really is the major venue operators' own storefront: operated by Showcatcher Ltd (company 07628569, led by Assembly founder William Burdett-Coutts) as a declared ticket agent for seven operators (Assembly, C ARTS, Gilded Balloon, Just the Tonic, Pleasance, Underbelly, ZOO) on Red61 rails — so it covers only those venues' shows, never the full ~3,600-show catalogue.
3. Since March 2025 edfringe.com and the official app run on equ's Tikketr platform (the API the repo scrapes) as an explicitly interim system — Red61 ran the Society's ticketing until 2023/24 and still powers the venue operators' own box offices, and a permanent Storm ID-built site is due for Fringe 2027, meaning the scrape target is likely to change again and remains the only single source covering every registered show.

===== api_documentation_fringe_approval (4444 chars) =====
 Fringe listings | Edinburgh Festivals Listings API Contact us Toggle navigation Edinburgh Festivals Listings API Explore Docs Projects Listings widget Contact us Login / Register Overview Fringe approval Genre representation Ticketing Data freshness Requesting approval Access to Fringe listings All developers wishing to use the live Fringe data will have to build their applications using a demonstration dataset and submit them for review to ensure that they are complying with the relevant licence terms and presenting the data appropriately. This is particularly because many application developers will not have had experience with the particularities of Fringe ticketing and listings and therefore may not be sensitive to all the nuances of presenting and interpreting Fringe listings data in the way audiences expect. In addition to general licence compliance, the review team will be checking the following points prior to granting approval. Genre representation The Fringe is passionate about ensuring all types of performers from all backgrounds have equal position within the festival – it is part of what makes the Fringe so special. Therefore we strongly encourage apps to not cover individual genres alone. Ticketing information The vast majority of applications should simply display the price and concession prices for Fringe performances and use the website parameter to deep-link to full event and ticketing information on the Fringe website. If you intend to use the more detailed response properties to show additional pricing, discount or concession information within your application we strongly advise you to discuss usage and requirements with us in advance, and we will check these details are being displayed correctly before approving live data access. Please note that under the terms of the licence you must only use the links to edfringe.com provided by the API and must not link to any other ticketing site (including the venue's own site) from any content provided through the API. Data Freshness Festival listings data changes regularly throughout the year and in particular over the summer. To ensure your application is displaying accurate information, you should retrieve fresh data from the API at least every 24 hours. Please note that for performance reasons we do encourage caching of listings data - on your own servers and/or on client devices - so long as you refresh your cache regularly. You can use the last_modified query parameter to retrieve events that have changed since your the last update. For devices that may not have a permanent internet connection (eg iPod touch) you should include a mechanism to alert the user when the data may be out of date. Requesting Approval The Fringe approval process is not intended to be a hurdle, but we do want to ensure that the data is being used and presented accurately and consistently so as to avoid confusion for visitors and Fringe participants. For anything other than simple projects, you may wish to contact us before beginning work on your application to discuss your proposed usage. To discuss your plans, or to request Fringe API access for an existing application, please contact us and provide as much information as possible, including: the email you used to register for the API a contact phone number a simple one-line description of the application a description of how your application will display and interpret the data any relevant URLs and screenshots etc After you have received ini

 Projects | Edinburgh Festivals Listings API Contact us Toggle navigation Edinburgh Festivals Listings API Explore Docs Projects Listings widget Contact us Login / Register Projects A collection of some of the projects built using the Edinburgh Festivals Listings API. Fringe Vibes Fringe Vibes by Tavish provides a new visual way to discover shows at the Fringe. It will curate a selection of shows based on your search query using natural language, for example, "awkward standup comics", and displays events in a huge scrollable grid, allowing you to discover even more. FringeFlow FringeFlow uses AI to create a personalised show schedule so you can see more of what you like. TicketBadger TicketBadger is an AI-powered listings discovery tool that allows users to find the perfect event for their next trip to the Edinburgh Festivals. Plan My Fringe Plan My Fringe by Henson IT Solutions have developed a very innovative and powerful planning tool enabling visitors and avid Fringe-goers alike to find events and optimise a custom schedule helping them make the most of their visit. Their algorithm allows users to prioritise shows by rating the ones they want to see and takes into account walking time between venues, budgets and even allows time for lunch and sleep breaks! Transport for Edinburgh Transport for Edinburgh used the Edinburgh Festival Listings API to augment their travel assistance app with the festivals venue data allowing users to easily plan their journeys to or from festival venues. During the festivals, venues open across the city with new names and in all kinds of unusual locations. Utilising the venue data available through the API visitors can quickly find venues by their unique names or number making planning their journeys a lot easier. You can download the Transport for Edinburgh app here. Zegami Zegami was founded in 2016 after a successful collaboration between the Weatherall Institute of Molecular Medicine at the University of Oxford and was developed so that it could be used to visualise any kind of data, including images, video, documents or more traditional data sources like databases and spreadsheets. Zegami used the Edinburgh Festivals Listings API to demonstrate the power of their data visualisation platform. It allows users to easily explore large image datasets and unlock powerful insights through their advanced analysis tools with a unique visualisation interface. Find out more about Zegami . Frindr Frindr is a fun way to discover shows at the Fringe, swiping through a selection of shows, the app will attempt to suggest more of what you might like and help to curate a list of favourites to book. festies festies by Alan Nevens is a social bookmarking site for people to be able to keep track of festival shows they might want to see and to share these with their friends. myFestival myFestival is an iOS festival planner app developed by Mike Crawford. You can use your location to find events nearby, curate your list of favourites shared across your iOS devices, and add performances to the calendar on your device. Festival Clock The Edinburgh Festival Clock was a visualisation designed by Stefanie Posavec and developed by Justin Quillinan. Each event is represented by a line: the free shows are positioned on the outside of each festival circle, with the most expensive shows in the circle. By fast-forwarding the clock, one is able to quickly move through time and see how the festivals evolve through the season, showing

## EdFest.com Overview

EdFest.com is a unique collaboration between some of the Edinburgh Festival Fringe's leading venues, including Assembly, C ARTS, Gilded Balloon, Just the Tonic, Pleasance, Underbelly and ZOO, built by the venues that power the Fringe to bring shows together on a single, cross-venue platform.

## Showcatcher Connection

EdFest is powered by Showcatcher and is a gathering of eight of the core venues that present a world-class programme of shows as part of the Edinburgh Festival Fringe. Showcatcher serves as the technical ticket agent behind the platform.

## Launch Background

The collaboration was initiated in 2022 after the impact of the Covid pandemic that created a two-year hiatus for the Festival, with most of the EdFest venues operating at about ten percent of what they did pre-pandemic in 2021.

Audiences can browse comedy, theatre, circus, cabaret, dance, music, and family shows across multiple venues, then book tickets from different venues in a single basket, with booking fees capped at £5 per transaction.

## Ticket Allocation to Fringe Box Office

Performers are required to make at least the equivalent of 25% of their tickets per performance available to sell at the Fringe Box Office. This percentage can be increased when you fill in your Show Registration Form, or at any point during your run via the Box Office Reporting Portal.

## Commission on Ticket Sales

An administrative commission of 5% plus VAT is applied on the face value of all tickets sold through the Fringe Box Office. This represents a recent increase — the charity is increasing the cut it takes on sales from its box office from four to five per cent from next year.

## Fee Rebate Scheme

A fee rebate scheme has paid back £1.8m to producers and venues since 2022 which will now be less generous. The rebate is being maintained for 2025 but with a necessary reduction from a threshold of 60% to 50%.

## Venue Considerations

Many venues operate an on-site box office as well, and performers may choose to sell some tickets through the Fringe Box Office and the remainder through the venue by discussing allocation with their venue manager.

content.content:
# Registration with Official Edinburgh Festival Fringe

PBH's Free Fringe does **not require** performers to register with the official Edinburgh Festival Fringe Society programme. Registration is optional.

However, if performers choose to register, they must follow specific guidelines:

**Key requirement:** "If you choose to register your show with the Edinburgh Festival Fringe Society (EFFS), list your performer name as [your name]/PBH's Free Fringe."

Additionally, performers are strongly encouraged to become EFFS members (a separate, cheaper requirement costing £5) and to vote in Fringe Society board elections, as this aligns with the Free Fringe's political ethos of giving "performers' voices...at the heart of the whole fringe."

The Wee Blue Book serves as the Free Fringe's own comprehensive listing, independent of the official Fringe programme. Performers receive "a free listing" in this publication when they submit their show description and image.

findings.fact: The Edinburgh Festivals Listings API is 'a free-to-use API to the official event listings database for Edinburgh's 11 major Festivals' with 'over 640,000 performances and growing'; it is 'A project created by Edinburgh's Festivals... managed by inGenerator. Operated by Festivals Edinburgh Limited' (Scottish company SC331673).

Live Fringe data on the Listings API is approval-gated: developers must build against a 'demofringe' dummy dataset ('all titles, copy and similar text content has been randomised') and submit the app for review; the review checks genre representation ('we strongly encourage apps to not cover individual genres alone') and ticketing presentation.

Fringe licence terms on the Listings API state: 'you must only use the links to edfringe.com provided by the API and must not link to any other ticketing site (including the venue's own site) from any content provided through the API' - so an API-based product cannot deep-link to venue box offices.

Listings API licence: commercial use is permitted ('for any lawful purpose, including commercial applications'), attribution is required, redistribution of feeds/dumps to third parties is forbidden, data must be refreshed at least every 24 hours, and Festivals Edinburgh may terminate and require deletion of all listings data.

The Events API returns per-performance 'start'/'end' times, 'price'/'concession'/'price_string', 'duration_minutes', and an event 'status' of active/cancelled/deleted, but no sold-out or availability field; sync uses 'modified_from' with 'a delay of a few minutes between an event being marked as modified and it being returned in an API query', indicating a near-real-time update pipeline from the source database.
The API explorer publicly offers festival=fringe with Year options through 2026, indicating the Fringe 2026 programme is loaded; festival_id values cover all 11 festivals plus demofringe.

The API's projects page showcases currently-listed third-party Fringe discovery/planner apps built on it - Fringe Vibes, FringeFlow, TicketBadger, Plan My Fringe (schedule optimiser with walking times) - showing that approval is actively granted to products functionally similar to EdFringeNow.
The Listings API now exposes a beta MCP endpoint (https://api.edinburghfestivalcity.com/mcp, Bearer-token auth, max 100 events per request, minimal summary data) for AI agents.
Laughing Horse Free Festival shows are necessarily in the official database: 'All of our shows must be entered into the Official Fringe Programme.'

PBH's Free Fringe makes official Fringe registration optional ('If you choose to register your show with the Edinburgh Festival Fringe Society (EFFS)...'), and runs its own independent Wee Blue Book listing - so some PBH shows exist in neither edfringe.com nor the Listings API.

Assembly (assemblyfestival.com) has no public listings API: its site is a Nuxt app whose server-rendered payload embeds event records with red61_event_id/red61_venue_id/raw_data fields (synced from Red61 ticketing) from a Directus CMS at assemblyfestival.pazaz.studio, which returns 403 FORBIDDEN ('You don't have permission to access collection \"events\"') to anonymous API requests; /wp-json and /api/* paths just return the app shell HTML.

Gilded Balloon runs WordPress with an open /wp-json REST API, but its registered post types (posts, pages, jobs, venues, etc.) include no show/event/performance type, so show listings are not machine-readable there.

Pleasance (www.pleasance.co.uk) is Drupal with JSON:API disabled (/jsonapi returns 404) and no JSON-LD on event pages; Underbelly (underbellyedinburgh.co.uk) and The Stand (www.thestand.co.uk) render event listings only as server-side HTML with no JSON-LD, no /api endpoints and no iCal/ics feeds; Monkey Barrel is a Wix site (hashed Wix .json bundles only); Summerhall returns HTTP 403 to non-browser clients. No probed venue operator publishes any public machine-readable listings feed.

Data Thistle (The List's events-data arm) aggregates listings from venues, festival organisers and 26+ integrated ticketing partners (Ticketmaster, See Tickets, Spektrix), explicitly offers 'Edinburgh Festival' data among its products, distributes to media including The List and Reach PLC, and sells access via an 'Events API' - but publishes no pricing; commercial licensing is by contact only.

Skiddle's developer Events API is 'still in Beta' and 'for non-commercial use only'; Skiddle runs a separate ticket affiliate programme, and its Edinburgh Fringe presence is a festival landing page rather than the full registered programme.

WeGotTickets' Edinburgh/Scotland region search returned about 30 events with zero mentioning the Fringe (checked 2026-07-31, a week before the festival), and Eventbrite's 'edinburgh-fringe' search surfaces only scattered unofficial free-comedy events (e.g. 'Edinburgh Fringe Free Comedy 22:35 Every Night on Cowgate') - neither carries the registered programme.

Ents24 operates an authenticated REST API to a ~100,000-event UK live-entertainment database with comedy/theatre genre filtering (docs at developers.ents24.com), but no evidence was found that it carries substantial Edinburgh Fringe programme coverage; its Fringe landing URLs 404.

Registration on edfringe.com is what puts a show in the official programme (2026: 3,649 shows across 258 venues), and Fringe Society communications confirm free-show operators' registered shows 'are listed on edfringe.com and in the official Fringe app' - so the official database (and hence the Listings API's fringe feed) and edfringe.com share the same registered-show universe.

keyClaims: No public machine-readable source other than edfringe.com's own GraphQL exposes per-performance ticket-availability/sold-out status - the official Listings API, all venue-operator sites, and all aggregators lack it - so any availability feature requires continuing to hit edfringe.com in some form.

The official Edinburgh Festivals Listings API's fringe feed is the official registered-show catalogue (same universe as edfringe.com, 2026 data live, per-performance times/prices, near-real-time modified pipeline) and is the only licensed, free replacement for the catalogue scrape - but it is gated by an app-approval process and its licence forbids linking to any ticketing site other than edfringe.com.

No venue operator publishes a public listings API or feed (Assembly's Directus CMS is locked, Gilded Balloon's open wp-json has no show type, the rest are HTML-only/Wix/403), and no commercial aggregator offers usable full-programme Fringe coverage except Data Thistle, which is paid, contact-for-pricing.
openQuestions: Whether the Listings API licence permits combining its Fringe catalogue with availability data scraped separately from edfringe.com's Tikketr GraphQL in the same product - the licence and approval docs don't address mixed sources, and approval review might object.

The exact upstream pipeline in the Tikketr era: whether the Listings API is now fed directly from the Tikketr platform database or via a Fringe Society export, and what real-world lag (minutes vs hours) exists between an edfringe.com change (price, cancellation, added performance) and its appearance in the API during August.
Data Thistle's actual per-performance depth for Fringe shows (does it carry every performance time and edfringe ticket links?) and its API pricing - both are contact-only.
Whether Ents24 carries any meaningful subset of Fringe listings (its API requires registration to query; no public Fringe pages found).
How many PBH Free Fringe shows skip official registration each year (i.e. the size of the gap that neither edfringe.com nor the Listings API covers).

Whether Fringe approval for the Listings API would be granted to a product that also displays availability/sold-out badges sourced elsewhere, and how long the approval process takes (not stated in the docs).

input.summary: Nothing publicly available can fully replace the edfringe.com GraphQL scrape, because no other machine-readable source exposes per-performance ticket availability; but the official Edinburgh Festivals Listings API (api.edinburghfestivalcity.com, operated by Festivals Edinburgh Ltd, managed by inGenerator) is a viable licensed backbone for the catalogue itself. Its Fringe feed is the official registered-show database (the same universe as edfringe.com's ~3,649 registered shows, including Laughing Horse Free Festival shows, which must register, and most PBH Free Fringe shows, for which registration is optional), with per-performance start/end/price, cancelled/deleted status, a near-real-time last_modified sync pipeline ("a delay of a few minutes"), a 24h minimum refresh rule, 2026 data live in its explorer, and even a beta MCP endpoint - but no sold-out/availability field, a mandatory app-approval process using a demofringe dummy dataset, and a hard licence rule that you may only link to edfringe.com URLs supplied by the API (never venue or other ticketing sites). Its projects page shows it actively approves discovery/planner apps nearly identical to EdFringeNow (Fringe Vibes, FringeFlow, TicketBadger, Plan My Fringe). Direct probing of all seven major venue-operator sites found no public machine-readable listings anywhere: Assembly runs a Nuxt front-end fed by a locked Directus CMS (assemblyfestival.pazaz.studio returns 403 anonymously) that syncs from Red61 ticketing; Gilded Balloon's open wp-json exposes no show/event post type; Pleasance (Drupal), Underbelly and The Stand render listings only as server-side HTML with no JSON-LD; Monkey Barrel is a Wix site; Summerhall 403s non-browser clients; no iCal/ics feeds exist on any of them. Among aggregators, Data Thistle (The List's data arm) is the only one with real festival coverage - it explicitly sells "Edinburgh Festival" events data via a commercial API with no published pricing - while Skiddle's API is beta and non-commercial-only with thin Fringe coverage, Eventbrite carries only stray unregistered free-comedy events, WeGotTickets' Edinburgh region search shows zero Fringe listings, and Ents24's authenticated API has unverified (likely minimal) Fringe coverage. Bottom line ranking: (1) official Listings API for the full catalogue (free, licensed, stable, but availability-blind and approval-gated); (2) continued edfringe GraphQL scraping, reduced to an availability/sold-out overlay if the API is adopted; (3) Data Thistle only if paying for a commercial licence makes sense; (4) per-venue feeds and other aggregators are not viable at all. The practical combination is official API catalogue + a slimmed edfringe availability probe, noting the unresolved licence question of blending scraped availability with API data.

PBH's Free Fringe makes official Fringe registration optional ('If you choose to register your show with the Edinburgh Festival Fringe Society (EFFS)...'), and runs its own independent Wee Blue Book listing - so some PBH shows exist in neither edfringe.com nor the Listings API.

Assembly (assemblyfestival.com) has no public listings API: its site is a Nuxt app whose server-rendered payload embeds event records with red61_event_id/red61_venue_id/raw_data fields (synced from Red61 ticketing) from a Directus CMS at assemblyfestival.pazaz.studio, which returns 403 FORBIDDEN ('You don't have permission to access collection \"events\"') to anonymous API requests; /wp-json and /api/* paths just return the app shell HTML.

Gilded Balloon runs WordPress with an open /wp-json REST API, but its registered post types (posts, pages, jobs, venues, etc.) include no show/event/performance type, so show listings are not machine-readable there.

Pleasance (www.pleasance.co.uk) is Drupal with JSON:API disabled (/jsonapi returns 404) and no JSON-LD on event pages; Underbelly (underbellyedinburgh.co.uk) and The Stand (www.thestand.co.uk) render event listings only as server-side HTML with no JSON-LD, no /api endpoints and no iCal/ics feeds; Monkey Barrel is a Wix site (hashed Wix .json bundles only); Summerhall returns HTTP 403 to non-browser clients. No probed venue operator publishes any public machine-readable listings feed.

Data Thistle (The List's events-data arm) aggregates listings from venues, festival organisers and 26+ integrated ticketing partners (Ticketmaster, See Tickets, Spektrix), explicitly offers 'Edinburgh Festival' data among its products, distributes to media including The List and Reach PLC, and sells access via an 'Events API' - but publishes no pricing; commercial licensing is by contact only.

Skiddle's developer Events API is 'still in Beta' and 'for non-commercial use only'; Skiddle runs a separate ticket affiliate programme, and its Edinburgh Fringe presence is a festival landing page rather than the full registered programme.

WeGotTickets' Edinburgh/Scotland region search returned about 30 events with zero mentioning the Fringe (checked 2026-07-31, a week before the festival), and Eventbrite's 'edinburgh-fringe' search surfaces only scattered unofficial free-comedy events (e.g. 'Edinburgh Fringe Free Comedy 22:35 Every Night on Cowgate') - neither carries the registered programme.

Ents24 operates an authenticated REST API to a ~100,000-event UK live-entertainment database with comedy/theatre genre filtering (docs at developers.ents24.com), but no evidence was found that it carries substantial Edinburgh Fringe programme coverage; its Fringe landing URLs 404.

Registration on edfringe.com is what puts a show in the official programme (2026: 3,649 shows across 258 venues), and Fringe Society communications confirm free-show operators' registered shows 'are listed on edfringe.com and in the official Fringe app' - so the official database (and hence the Listings API's fringe feed) and edfringe.com share the same registered-show universe.

keyClaims: No public machine-readable source other than edfringe.com's own GraphQL exposes per-performance ticket-availability/sold-out status - the official Listings API, all venue-operator sites, and all aggregators lack it - so any availability feature requires continuing to hit edfringe.com in some form.

The official Edinburgh Festivals Listings API's fringe feed is the official registered-show catalogue (same universe as edfringe.com, 2026 data live, per-performance times/prices, near-real-time modified pipeline) and is the only licensed, free replacement for the catalogue scrape - but it is gated by an app-approval process and its licence forbids linking to any ticketing site other than edfringe.com.

No venue operator publishes a public listings API or feed (Assembly's Directus CMS is locked, Gilded Balloon's open wp-json has no show type, the rest are HTML-only/Wix/403), and no commercial aggregator offers usable full-programme Fringe coverage except Data Thistle, which is paid, contact-for-pricing.
openQuestions: Whether the Listings API licence permits combining its Fringe catalogue with availability data scraped separately from edfringe.com's Tikketr GraphQL in the same product - the licence and approval docs don't address mixed sources, and approval review might object.

The exact upstream pipeline in the Tikketr era: whether the Listings API is now fed directly from the Tikketr platform database or via a Fringe Society export, and what real-world lag (minutes vs hours) exists between an edfringe.com change (price, cancellation, added performance) and its appearance in the API during August.
Data Thistle's actual per-performance depth for Fringe shows (does it carry every performance time and edfringe ticket links?) and its API pricing - both are contact-only.
Whether Ents24 carries any meaningful subset of Fringe listings (its API requires registration to query; no public Fringe pages found).
How many PBH Free Fringe shows skip official registration each year (i.e. the size of the gap that neither edfringe.com nor the Listings API covers).

Whether Fringe approval for the Listings API would be granted to a product that also displays availability/sold-out badges sourced elsewhere, and how long the approval process takes (not stated in the docs).

CONTEXT (shared by all researchers):
You are researching for EdFringeNow, a client-side web product for the Edinburgh Festival Fringe (discovery + trip planner). The repo currently gets its show catalogue by scraping edfringe.com's GraphQL API (Tikketr platform, edfringe-tikketr-web-api.equhost.com) nightly via GitHub Actions. The owner wants to understand how Fringe tickets are ACTUALLY sold, who all the "event providers" (venue operators) are, whether a third party can sell tickets itself (affiliate/agent/API), and whether provider or aggregator listings APIs could replace the edfringe scrape.

TODAY is 2026-07-31. The 2026 Fringe runs 7-31 August (3,649 shows, 258 venues). Prefer 2025/2026 sources; older sources are fine for structural facts if you say so.

TOOLING CONSTRAINTS: You have WebSearch and WebFetch. edfringe.com returns 403 to WebFetch and equhost.com is blocked by the egress proxy - for those domains rely on WebSearch result snippets and third-party coverage. Most other sites (venue operators, news, wikis) are fetchable; if a fetch fails, fall back to search. Cite EVERY fact with a real URL you actually saw.

OUTPUT: your final output is consumed by a script, not a human. Fill the schema honestly: mark confidence low when a claim rests on one thin source; put what you could NOT establish into openQuestions rather than guessing. keyClaims = the 2-3 claims your topic's conclusions rest on (the ones that, if wrong, change the product decision).

You are an ADVERSARIAL fact-checker. A researcher investigating "operators" for the Edinburgh Fringe ticketing landscape rests their conclusions on the claims below. Your job is to try to REFUTE each claim with your own independent web searches - do not reuse the researcher's sources as confirmation; find your own. A claim is "confirmed" only if independent evidence supports it; "plausible" if consistent with what you found but not independently confirmed; "refuted" if you found contrary evidence (then write the correction); "unverifiable" if the public record genuinely doesn't settle it. Be especially suspicious of: ownership claims (who runs/owns a website), "no such scheme exists" negatives (search for the scheme yourself before agreeing), and platform/vendor claims (which ticketing tech powers which site).

CLAIMS:
1. The big commercial Fringe operators all sell the same shows on their own box-office sites in parallel with edfringe.com, and at least 10 of the 15 major operators (Assembly, Pleasance, Underbelly, Gilded Balloon, Summerhall, ZOO, C ARTS, theSpaceUK, Just the Tonic, Scottish Storytelling Centre) run those channels on a single shared platform: Red61 VIA, mostly as *.online.red61.co.uk white-labels with N:XXXX composite event IDs.
2. Parallel selling is governed by a published Fringe Society rule — a minimum 25% of each performance's tickets must be allocated to the Fringe Box Office (5%+VAT commission) — and Summerhall's published pack quantifies the real-world split at typically 70% edfringe / 30% venue box office, meaning edfringe.com is the majority sales channel and the only complete catalogue.
3. The exceptions are few and identifiable — Traverse (Spektrix), The Stand (in-house), Monkey Barrel (Line-Up/liveit.io, Fringe runs via edfringe), Greenside (edfringe-only), Dance Base (via Assembly) — so venue/provider APIs alone can never cover the full show catalogue, and any provider-side data or affiliate strategy is essentially a question about access to Red61 VIA.
