- generate-project-instructions: Decompose a project into its pack facets (working-style class, technology, aspect, domain) and extract its working instructions into reusable canon packs plus the project's own local packs (.claudinite/local_packs/). Use when a project has no established working style yet, or it exhibits a facet no pack covers — during bootstrap of a fresh/empty repo, or on an uplevel request.
- git-github-advanced: Git/GitHub procedures beyond the baseline lifecycle. Use for commit layering, recovering a branch after a squash-merge, CI-trigger rules, GitHub Actions gotchas, or merge-relocation traps.
- github-actions-scheduling: What a GitHub Actions `schedule:` trigger actually guarantees — late fires, dropped fires, the 60-day disable — and how to build and describe scheduled work around it. Use when adding, changing, explaining, or debugging anything that runs on a cron in GitHub Actions.
- merge-to-main: Merge the change in front of the owner into main. Use when the owner says "LGTM" or asks to merge/land the current branch or PR into main.
- probe-edfringe-api: Get a fact out of the live edfringe.com GraphQL API (a field's real shape, an enum's full value set, one show's payload) from a session that cannot reach it, by running a throwaway probe on a GitHub Actions runner. Use when scraper/SCRAPING.md doesn't already record the answer and guessing would be a guess.
- prose-to-checks: Mine a repo's existing pack prose (RULES.md, SKILL.md) for always-testable rules that were never converted to checks, and convert the strongest ones. Use when auditing packs for convertible rules, or when the growth prose-to-checks sweep runs.
- repo-text-sweeps: Mechanics for grep/sed sweeps, renames, and path relocations across a repo. Use before a bulk find-replace, a rename, or moving files — and after one, to catch silently broken references.
- single-branch-status: Assess one branch's landed status — merged, already-in-main, superseded, orphaned, or genuine unmerged work — read-only. Use when triaging whether a single branch is safe to delete, judging by content not the ref's name (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-branches task hands you branches to assess).
- single-issue-triage: Triage one open issue and take the first applicable action — close-if-implemented, needs-decision, blocked, quick-win, or leave. Use when acting on a single issue; "implemented in main" must be verified against main's current content and the default is to comment, not close (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-issues task hands you issues to triage).
- single-pr-status: Assess one open pull request's landed status — keep-open, or closeable (merged, already-in-main, superseded, stale) — read-only. Use when triaging whether a single PR should stay open, judging by its commits and diff not its title (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-prs task hands you PRs to assess).
- unattended-agents: Architecture and practices for unattended, automation-invoked agents and recurring routines. Use when building, structuring, or running an AI agent, a scheduled routine, or a multi-stage agent pipeline.
- writing-tests: Practices for writing tests you can trust. Use before writing or changing any test — see-it-fail discipline, snapshot/golden rules, CI-only and heavy-browser tests, fuzzy-metric gating.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".

- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

## Key Issues and Timeline

An open letter campaign was instigated after the Fringe Society dropped its official smartphone app, and was backed by major venue operators including Assembly, Gilded Balloon, Just the Tonic, the PBH Free Fringe and Underbelly.

William Burdett-Coutts, artistic director of Assembly who has been staging shows for more than 40 years, accused the Fringe Society of failing to plan properly and virtually ignoring the venues who put on the bulk of its programme.

He suggested the charity had under-estimated demand, cut back on key services for venues and artists, while being "obsessed" with the future values of the festival at the expense of ensuring its survival.

## Ticketing Alliance

Assembly is one of eight Fringe venue operators involved in a new alliance which launched its own website to sell tickets ahead of the launch of the official programme.

## Recent Communication Concerns

More recently, Burdett-Coutts stated that "the lack of communication between the Fringe Society and Fringe venues is a serious failure" and that "the people that make the Fringe happen deserve a voice at the table."

Based on the search results, here's what I found regarding Edinburgh Fringe ticketing when shows appear sold out:

When a performance shows "This performance has no ticket allocation remaining," it means the Fringe Box Office allocation has sold out. However, there's an important distinction: if the message says "Please check with the venue box office for further ticket allocation," tickets may still be available.

The key reason for this is that artists may choose to sell some tickets through the Fringe Box Office and the remainder through the venue – discussing how to allocate tickets with the venue manager. 

Additionally, venues can allocate additional tickets to the Fringe Box Office at any time, so it's worth checking back now and then to see if a show has available tickets.

So in summary, even if a show appears sold out on the Fringe Box Office system, it's important to check with the venue box office directly, as they'll have the most up to date information.

Red61's clients include Edinburgh Festival Fringe, Assembly, Gilded Balloon, Pleasance, Underbelly, Edinburgh International Science Festival, Edinburgh International Book Festival, Edinburgh's Christmas, Edinburgh's Hogmanay, National Arts Festival South Africa, Toronto Fringe Festival, and Garden of Unearthly Delights (Adelaide).

Red61 was founded in 2002 to build a robust and flexible ticketing system that could handle the size and complexity of the Edinburgh Festival Fringe. verdicts.claim: edfringe.com is run by the Edinburgh Festival Fringe Society — an independent, membership-governed registered charity and company limited by guarantee that no venue operator owns or controls (they have publicly feuded with it) — and its box office sells each show under an allocation model (minimum 25% of tickets per performance, 5%+VAT commission), with NO_ALLOCATION_CONTACT_VENUE meaning the central allocation is exhausted but the venue's own Red61 box office may still have tickets.
verdicts.correction: Two small precision notes, not refutations: the enum string NO_ALLOCATION_CONTACT_VENUE itself appears nowhere on the public web (it is only observable in the Tikketr API the repo scrapes), so its semantics are an inference — a well-supported one given the edfringe FAQ language. And 'the venue's own Red61 box office' is over-specific: the big operators' box offices are on Red61 (verified live), but not every one of the ~258 venues runs Red61, so read it as 'the venue's own box office (Red61 for the major operators)'.
verdicts.why: Every load-bearing element independently checks out. Companies House shows Edinburgh Festival Fringe Society Limited as a private company limited by guarantee WITHOUT share capital (so nobody can 'own' it), incorporated 22 May 1969, company SC046605 (https://find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/company/SC046605), registered Scottish charity SC002995 (https://findthatcharity.uk/orgid/GB-SC-SC002995); the Society's own pages say members (any individual, £5/yr) elect the Board at the AGM (https://www.edfringe.com/about-us/the-fringe-society/fringe-society-membership/). The public feud with venue operators is well documented: an open letter 'rebellion' backed by Assembly, Gilded Balloon, Just the Tonic, PBH Free Fringe and Underbelly after the Society dropped its app (https://www.scotsman.com/whats-on/arts-and-entertainment/open-letter-sparks-rebellion-over-running-of-the-edinburgh-festival-fringe-3756226), Assembly's William Burdett-Coutts saying he had 'lost confidence' in the Society (https://www.scotsman.com/whats-on/arts-and-entertainment/edinburgh-festival-fringe-longest-running-venue-operator-says-he-has-lost-confidence-in-the-fringe-society-3791322) and warning of a 'serious failure' in communication (https://www.scotsman.com/arts-and-culture/serious-failure-in-communication-between-venues-and-fringe-society-assembly-founder-warns-5285657). The allocation model is confirmed by the Fringe's own registration help pages: performers must make at least 25% of tickets per performance available to the Fringe Box Office, with a 5%+VAT administrative commission on face value (https://help.registration.edfringe.com/create-or-edit-a-show/payout-and-fringe-allocation.aspx); Chortle independently reported the commission rising from 4% to 5% for 2025 (https://www.chortle.co.uk/news/2024/12/13/57178/edinburgh_fringe_society_hikes_its_ticket_commission_25%25, https://www.edfringe.com/about-us/news-and-blog/changes-to-2025-rebate-and-commission-structures/). The enum interpretation matches the Fringe's own FAQ wording — 'this performance has no ticket allocation remaining… check with the venue box office for further ticket allocation', and venues can top up the central allocation at any time (https://www.edfringe.com/faqs/) — and the repo's own scrape data (scraper/SCRAPING.md, e.g. Daniel Sloss soldOut:false + ticketStatus:NO_ALLOCATION_CONTACT_VENUE) shows the enum behaving exactly this way.

verdicts.claim: edfest.com is the major venue operators' own storefront: operated by Showcatcher Ltd (company 07628569, led by Assembly founder William Burdett-Coutts) as a declared ticket agent for seven operators (Assembly, C ARTS, Gilded Balloon, Just the Tonic, Pleasance, Underbelly, ZOO) on Red61 rails — so it covers only those venues' shows, never the full ~3,600-show catalogue.
verdicts.correction: One wording caveat: I could not find an explicit 'we act as ticket agent for the venues' declaration in edfest.com's current or archived terms/FAQs — Showcatcher Ltd is clearly the operator selling the seven operators' inventory (functionally an agent), but 'declared ticket agent' overstates what the public terms literally say. Also note the roster has shifted over time: 2022 launch coverage described 'eight' venues (https://theedinburghreporter.co.uk/2022/06/edfest-platform-a-one-stop-shop-for-tickets-from-eight-fringe-venues/); seven is the current 2026 lineup.
verdicts.why: Companies House confirms SHOWCATCHER LTD, company 07628569, active, incorporated 10 May 2011, SIC 'support activities to performing arts' (https://find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/company/07628569), with William Walter Burdett-Coutts a director since incorporation (https://find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/company/07628569/officers); he is Assembly's founder/artistic director per Scotsman coverage and https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Burdett-Coutts_(promoter). CONTEXT (shared by all researchers):
You are researching for EdFringeNow, a client-side web product for the Edinburgh Festival Fringe (discovery + trip planner). The repo currently gets its show catalogue by scraping edfringe.com's GraphQL API (Tikketr platform, edfringe-tikketr-web-api.equhost.com) nightly via GitHub Actions. The owner wants to understand how Fringe tickets are ACTUALLY sold, who all the "event providers" (venue operators) are, whether a third party can sell tickets itself (affiliate/agent/API), and whether provider or aggregator listings APIs could replace the edfringe scrape.

TODAY is 2026-07-31. The 2026 Fringe runs 7-31 August (3,649 shows, 258 venues). Prefer 2025/2026 sources; older sources are fine for structural facts if you say so.

TOOLING CONSTRAINTS: You have WebSearch and WebFetch. edfringe.com returns 403 to WebFetch and equhost.com is blocked by the egress proxy - for those domains rely on WebSearch result snippets and third-party coverage. Most other sites (venue operators, news, wikis) are fetchable; if a fetch fails, fall back to search. Cite EVERY fact with a real URL you actually saw.

OUTPUT: your final output is consumed by a script, not a human. Fill the schema honestly: mark confidence low when a claim rests on one thin source; put what you could NOT establish into openQuestions rather than guessing. keyClaims = the 2-3 claims your topic's conclusions rest on (the ones that, if wrong, change the product decision).

You are an ADVERSARIAL fact-checker. A researcher investigating "free-tail" for the Edinburgh Fringe ticketing landscape rests their conclusions on the claims below. Your job is to try to REFUTE each claim with your own independent web searches - do not reuse the researcher's sources as confirmation; find your own. A claim is "confirmed" only if independent evidence supports it; "plausible" if consistent with what you found but not independently confirmed; "refuted" if you found contrary evidence (then write the correction); "unverifiable" if the public record genuinely doesn't settle it. Be especially suspicious of: ownership claims (who runs/owns a website), "no such scheme exists" negatives (search for the scheme yourself before agreeing), and platform/vendor claims (which ticketing tech powers which site).

CLAIMS:
1. The official edfringe catalogue is the exhaustive universe of REGISTERED shows and venues (open-access festival, but paid show registration + free venue registration with the Fringe Society are what put you 'in the Fringe'), and the venue directory is enumerable both on tickets.edfringe.com/venues and via the API's VenueTypeAhead (301 records for 2026) — no active venue association offers a better list.
2. There is one demonstrable gap in that universe: Fringe Society registration is optional for PBH Free Fringe acts ('It's not compulsory to be in the program'), and PBH's own 2026 site lists ~795 entries across 50+ spaces versus only 183 PBH shows in the edfringe catalogue — so a large slice of the unticketed free programme lives only on freefringe.org.uk / the Wee Blue Book.
3. Free shows that ARE registered appear in edfringe data like any other show — FREE_NON_TICKETED (all 183 PBH shows), FREE_TICKETED (23 shows, non-PBH/LH), and Laughing Horse PWYC shows as ordinary TICKETS_AVAILABLE tickets sold through the Fringe Box Office — so the existing scrape already covers everything sellable, and the free-show operators present zero third-party ticket-selling opportunity (PBH has nothing to sell; Laughing Horse PWYC routes through the official box office).

texts = []

    chunk = m.group(1)
    try:
        d = zlib.decompress(chunk)
        if b'Tj' in d or b'TJ' in d:
            texts.append(d)
    except Exception:

full = b'\n'.join(texts).decode('latin-1', 'ignore')

        break
EOF

verdicts.claim: The big commercial Fringe operators all sell the same shows on their own box-office sites in parallel with edfringe.com, and at least 10 of 15 major operators (Assembly, Pleasance, Underbelly, Gilded Balloon, Summerhall, ZOO, C ARTS, theSpaceUK, Just the Tonic, Scottish Storytelling Centre) run those channels on a single shared platform: Red61 VIA, mostly as *.online.red61.co.uk white-labels with N:XXXX composite event IDs.
verdicts.correction: Two details are wrong. (1) Hostname pattern: the channels are NOT mostly *.online.red61.co.uk white-labels. I tested those subdomains directly: assembly., pleasance., underbelly., gildedballoon., carts. and justthetonic.online.red61.co.uk all 302 to https://online.red61.co.uk/wp-signup.php?new=... (WordPress-multisite 'no such site' fallback), i.e. they do not exist. The live channels are custom domains mapped onto Red61's WordPress network (tickets.gildedballoon.co.uk, tickets.thespaceuk.com, tickets.zoofestival.co.uk, tickets.summerhallarts.co.uk, edinburgh.justthetonic.com, res.cthearts.com) or deep VIA integrations inside the operator's own CMS (Pleasance /via/basket on Drupal; Underbelly and Assembly custom front-ends). Only Scottish Storytelling Centre actually lives at an online.red61.co.uk hostname; summerhall.online.red61.co.uk and zoo/thespaceuk aliases exist but 301 to the custom domains. Note Summerhall's current domain is tickets.summerhallarts.co.uk (post-liquidation 'Summerhall Arts'); the old alias redirects to tickets.summerhall.co.uk. (2) ID format: composite event IDs are <numeric-operator-prefix>:<event-number> — 14:6104 (Gilded Balloon), 911:5210 (theSpaceUK), 124:1938 (ZOO), 88:5403 (Just the Tonic), 34:3397 (C ARTS), 913:4655 (SSC), 61:9444 (Underbelly) — not a literal 'N:XXXX'. If 'N' was meant as a numeric placeholder the observation stands; as written it is misleading.
verdicts.why: I independently probed every named operator's live ticketing site (2026-07-31, all currently listing August 2026 Fringe shows) and found the shared Red61 VIA platform on all 10: tickets.gildedballoon.co.uk, tickets.thespaceuk.com, tickets.zoofestival.co.uk, edinburgh.justthetonic.com, res.cthearts.com (C ARTS), tickets.summerhallarts.co.uk and scottishstorytellingcentre.online.red61.co.uk all serve identical 'WordPress 7.0.2' + 'red61' + 'via-' markup with /event/<n>:<n> listings (e.g. https://tickets.gildedballoon.co.uk/events -> /event/14:6104; https://tickets.thespaceuk.com/events -> /event/911:5210; https://tickets.zoofestival.co.uk/events -> /event/124:1938; https://edinburgh.justthetonic.com/events -> /event/88:5403; https://res.cthearts.com/events -> /event/34:3397; https://scottishstorytellingcentre.online.red61.co.uk/events -> /event/913:4655). Pleasance's Drupal 10 site books through a Red61 VIA integration (event pages link to /via/basket, e.g. https://www.pleasance.co.uk/event/librarians-very-serious-comedy-fringe-preview); Underbelly's custom site books via /ticket-selection?event=61:9444&performance=61:187284 (https://www.underbellyedinburgh.co.uk/events/event/adam-riches-the-critics-way); Assembly's whats-on data layer carries red61_category_id / red61_venue_id fields (https://www.assemblyfestival.com/whats-on). Independent corroboration: Red61's own site names Edinburgh Festival Fringe, Assembly, Gilded Balloon, Pleasance and Underbelly as clients (https://www.red61.com/news/how-red61-can-maximise-your-sales-and-collaboration-efforts/, https://www.red61.com/news/red61-celebrates-20-years-at-the-edinburgh-festival-fringe/), and EdFest.com describes itself as the shared ticketing platform for Assembly, C ARTS, Gilded Balloon, Just the Tonic, Pleasance, Underbelly and ZOO with artist allocation managed 'through their red61 reporting site' (https://edfest.com/artists-producers, via search snippet; direct fetch 503). Parallel selling alongside edfringe.com is also stated by the Fringe's own FAQ: tickets can be bought at edfringe.com 'or through individual venue websites' (https://www.edfringe.com/faqs/).

verdicts.claim: Parallel selling is governed by a published Fringe Society rule — minimum 25% of each performance's tickets allocated to the Fringe Box Office at 5%+VAT commission — and Summerhall's published pack quantifies the split at typically 70% edfringe / 30% venue box office, making edfringe.com the majority sales channel and the only complete catalogue.
verdicts.correction: Minor scoping caveat: the 70/30 figure is Summerhall's typical split under its Full-Hire deal strand at one venue, not a published Fringe-wide statistic; the pack's other deal strand quotes a 4% Summerhall commission. Treating edfringe.com as the majority channel across ALL operators is an extrapolation from this one venue plus edfringe's softer 'half or more' statement — plausible, but no Fringe-wide sales-split figure is published.
verdicts.why: I fetched the primary sources myself. edfringe.com's ticketing page states verbatim: 'You are required to make at least the equivalent of 25% of your tickets per performance available to sell at the Fringe Box Office' and 'An administrative commission of 5% plus VAT is applied on the face value of all tickets sold' (https://www.edfringe.com/take-part/artists/organise-a-show/ticketing/). The 5% figure is current: the Fringe Society announced the increase from 4% (unchanged since 2013) to 5%+VAT for 2025 (https://www.edfringe.com/about-us/news-and-blog/changes-to-2025-rebate-and-commission-structures/). I downloaded the Summerhall Arts Festival Information Pack 2025 PDF and extracted the text directly: 'On the Full-Hire Agreement, The EdFringe Box Office Commission is 5%, and the Summerhall Arts Box Office Commission is 8%. Typically, 70% of tickets sold are through the EdFringe Box Office and 30% through the Summerhall Arts Box Office.' (https://www.summerhallarts.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/Summerhall-Arts-Festival-Information-Pack_2025_web.pdf). 'Only complete catalogue' is supported by the Fringe's own FAQ: the Fringe Box Office 'sells tickets for all shows registered with the Society' via counter, phone, edfringe.com and the app (https://www.edfringe.com/faqs/), and the ticketing page adds that 'many companies allocate half or more of their tickets to the Fringe Box Office'.

verdicts.claim: The exceptions are few and identifiable — Traverse (Spektrix), The Stand (in-house), Monkey Barrel (Line-Up/liveit.io, Fringe runs via edfringe), Greenside (edfringe-only), Dance Base (via Assembly) — so venue/provider APIs alone can never cover the full show catalogue, and any provider-side data or affiliate strategy is essentially a question about access to Red61 VIA.
verdicts.correction: The final strategic inference is too narrow. There is an official, currently-active non-Red61 route to the full Fringe catalogue that the claim ignores: the Fringe Society-sanctioned Edinburgh Festivals Listings API at https://api.edinburghfestivalcity.com/ — covering all 11 Edinburgh festivals including the Fringe, offering spreadsheet export, a public API, and an MCP server, 700,000+ performances since 2012, with a Fringe-approval process for live data (https://api.edinburghfestivalcity.com/documentation/fringe_approval). So a full-catalogue data strategy is a question about Fringe Society API approval at least as much as about Red61 VIA; Red61 access could only ever cover the commercial-operator subset. The same approval terms also cap any affiliate ambition: apps 'must only use the links to edfringe.com provided by the API and must not link to any other ticketing site' — i.e., the sanctioned third-party model is deep-linking to edfringe.com, not selling. Additionally, on the provider side there is already a Red61-run multi-operator aggregator, EdFest.com (Assembly, C ARTS, Gilded Balloon, Just the Tonic, Pleasance, Underbelly, ZOO — https://edfest.com/artists-producers), which is the more concrete 'Red61 access' surface than the individual venue white-labels.
verdicts.why: The exceptions list itself held up under my own probing. Traverse: Spektrix markers directly observed on https://www.traverse.co.uk/whats-on — CONFIRMED. The Stand: books on its own domain via /performance/<id>/... paths with cdn.thestand.co.uk assets and zero third-party platform markers (no Spektrix/Red61/Ticketsolve/Eventbrite) on https://www.thestand.co.uk/whats-on — consistent with in-house, though the underlying software vendor is unverifiable from outside. Monkey Barrel: 'Line-Up' branding plus booking.monkeybarrelcomedy.com and events.liveit.io links directly observed on https://www.monkeybarrelcomedy.com/ — CONFIRMED for club shows; its Fringe listings live on edfringe.com (dedicated page https://www.edfringe.com/experience/monkey-barrel-comedy-listings/) and its Wix Fringe pages expose no own-ticketing links, so 'Fringe via edfringe' is plausible but not airtight. Greenside: its GoDaddy-builder site (https://greensidevenue.co.uk/whats-on) has no ticket store, basket, or platform markers, consistent with edfringe-only, but I found no positive statement — unconfirmed. Dance Base: its own announcement says the festival is 'in partnership with Assembly Festival' with 'tickets on sale now from assemblyfestival.co.uk' (https://www.dancebase.co.uk/dance-base-and-assembly-announce-2025-edinburgh-festival-fringe-programme/, corroborated by https://www.broadwayworld.com/scotland/article/Dance-Base-and-Assembly-Reveal-2025-Edinburgh-Festival-Fringe-Programme-20250520) — CONFIRMED. 'Provider APIs alone can never cover the full catalogue' follows and is reinforced by my findings.

verdicts.claim: The big commercial Fringe operators all sell the same shows on their own box-office sites in parallel with edfringe.com, and at least 10 of 15 major operators (Assembly, Pleasance, Underbelly, Gilded Balloon, Summerhall, ZOO, C ARTS, theSpaceUK, Just the Tonic, Scottish Storytelling Centre) run those channels on a single shared platform: Red61 VIA, mostly as *.online.red61.co.uk white-labels with N:XXXX composite event IDs.
verdicts.why: I independently probed every named operator's live ticketing site (2026-07-31, all currently listing August 2026 Fringe shows) and found the shared Red61 VIA platform on all 10: tickets.gildedballoon.co.uk, tickets.thespaceuk.com, tickets.zoofestival.co.uk, edinburgh.justthetonic.com, res.cthearts.com (C ARTS), tickets.summerhallarts.co.uk and scottishstorytellingcentre.online.red61.co.uk all serve identical 'WordPress 7.0.2' + 'red61' + 'via-' markup with /event/<n>:<n> listings (e.g. https://tickets.gildedballoon.co.uk/events -> /event/14:6104; https://tickets.thespaceuk.com/events -> /event/911:5210; https://tickets.zoofestival.co.uk/events -> /event/124:1938; https://edinburgh.justthetonic.com/events -> /event/88:5403; https://res.cthearts.com/events -> /event/34:3397; https://scottishstorytellingcentre.online.red61.co.uk/events -> /event/913:4655). Pleasance's Drupal 10 site books through a Red61 VIA integration (event pages link to /via/basket, e.g. https://www.pleasance.co.uk/event/librarians-very-serious-comedy-fringe-preview); Underbelly's custom site books via /ticket-selection?event=61:9444&performance=61:187284 (https://www.underbellyedinburgh.co.uk/events/event/adam-riches-the-critics-way); Assembly's whats-on data layer carries red61_category_id / red61_venue_id fields (https://www.assemblyfestival.com/whats-on). Independent corroboration: Red61's own site names Edinburgh Festival Fringe, Assembly, Gilded Balloon, Pleasance and Underbelly as clients (https://www.red61.com/news/how-red61-can-maximise-your-sales-and-collaboration-efforts/, https://www.red61.com/news/red61-celebrates-20-years-at-the-edinburgh-festival-fringe/), and EdFest.com describes itself as the shared ticketing platform for Assembly, C ARTS, Gilded Balloon, Just the Tonic, Pleasance, Underbelly and ZOO with artist allocation managed 'through their red61 reporting site' (https://edfest.com/artists-producers, via search snippet; direct fetch 503). Parallel selling alongside edfringe.com is also stated by the Fringe's own FAQ: tickets can be bought at edfringe.com 'or through individual venue websites' (https://www.edfringe.com/faqs/).
verdicts.correction: Two details are wrong. (1) Hostname pattern: the channels are NOT mostly *.online.red61.co.uk white-labels. I tested those subdomains directly: assembly., pleasance., underbelly., gildedballoon., carts. and justthetonic.online.red61.co.uk all 302 to https://online.red61.co.uk/wp-signup.php?new=... (WordPress-multisite 'no such site' fallback), i.e. they do not exist. The live channels are custom domains mapped onto Red61's WordPress network (tickets.gildedballoon.co.uk, tickets.thespaceuk.com, tickets.zoofestival.co.uk, tickets.summerhallarts.co.uk, edinburgh.justthetonic.com, res.cthearts.com) or deep VIA integrations inside the operator's own CMS (Pleasance /via/basket on Drupal; Underbelly and Assembly custom front-ends). Only Scottish Storytelling Centre actually lives at an online.red61.co.uk hostname; summerhall.online.red61.co.uk and zoo/thespaceuk aliases exist but 301 to the custom domains. Note Summerhall's current domain is tickets.summerhallarts.co.uk (post-liquidation 'Summerhall Arts'); the old alias redirects to tickets.summerhall.co.uk. (2) ID format: composite event IDs are <numeric-operator-prefix>:<event-number> — 14:6104 (Gilded Balloon), 911:5210 (theSpaceUK), 124:1938 (ZOO), 88:5403 (Just the Tonic), 34:3397 (C ARTS), 913:4655 (SSC), 61:9444 (Underbelly) — not a literal 'N:XXXX'. If 'N' was meant as a numeric placeholder the observation stands; as written it is misleading.

verdicts.claim: Parallel selling is governed by a published Fringe Society rule — minimum 25% of each performance's tickets allocated to the Fringe Box Office at 5%+VAT commission — and Summerhall's published pack quantifies the split at typically 70% edfringe / 30% venue box office, making edfringe.com the majority sales channel and the only complete catalogue.
verdicts.why: I fetched the primary sources myself. edfringe.com's ticketing page states verbatim: 'You are required to make at least the equivalent of 25% of your tickets per performance available to sell at the Fringe Box Office' and 'An administrative commission of 5% plus VAT is applied on the face value of all tickets sold' (https://www.edfringe.com/take-part/artists/organise-a-show/ticketing/). The 5% figure is current: the Fringe Society announced the increase from 4% (unchanged since 2013) to 5%+VAT for 2025 (https://www.edfringe.com/about-us/news-and-blog/changes-to-2025-rebate-and-commission-structures/). I downloaded the Summerhall Arts Festival Information Pack 2025 PDF and extracted the text directly: 'On the Full-Hire Agreement, The EdFringe Box Office Commission is 5%, and the Summerhall Arts Box Office Commission is 8%. Typically, 70% of tickets sold are through the EdFringe Box Office and 30% through the Summerhall Arts Box Office.' (https://www.summerhallarts.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/Summerhall-Arts-Festival-Information-Pack_2025_web.pdf). 'Only complete catalogue' is supported by the Fringe's own FAQ: the Fringe Box Office 'sells tickets for all shows registered with the Society' via counter, phone, edfringe.com and the app (https://www.edfringe.com/faqs/), and the ticketing page adds that 'many companies allocate half or more of their tickets to the Fringe Box Office'.
verdicts.correction: Minor scoping caveat: the 70/30 figure is Summerhall's typical split under its Full-Hire deal strand at one venue, not a published Fringe-wide statistic; the pack's other deal strand quotes a 4% Summerhall commission. Treating edfringe.com as the majority channel across ALL operators is an extrapolation from this one venue plus edfringe's softer 'half or more' statement — plausible, but no Fringe-wide sales-split figure is published.

CONTEXT (shared by all researchers):
You are researching for EdFringeNow, a client-side web product for the Edinburgh Festival Fringe (discovery + trip planner). The repo currently gets its show catalogue by scraping edfringe.com's GraphQL API (Tikketr platform, edfringe-tikketr-web-api.equhost.com) nightly via GitHub Actions. The owner wants to understand how Fringe tickets are ACTUALLY sold, who all the "event providers" (venue operators) are, whether a third party can sell tickets itself (affiliate/agent/API), and whether provider or aggregator listings APIs could replace the edfringe scrape.

TODAY is 2026-07-31. The 2026 Fringe runs 7-31 August (3,649 shows, 258 venues). Prefer 2025/2026 sources; older sources are fine for structural facts if you say so.

TOOLING CONSTRAINTS: You have WebSearch and WebFetch. edfringe.com returns 403 to WebFetch and equhost.com is blocked by the egress proxy - for those domains rely on WebSearch result snippets and third-party coverage. Most other sites (venue operators, news, wikis) are fetchable; if a fetch fails, fall back to search. Cite EVERY fact with a real URL you actually saw.

OUTPUT: your final output is consumed by a script, not a human. Fill the schema honestly: mark confidence low when a claim rests on one thin source; put what you could NOT establish into openQuestions rather than guessing. keyClaims = the 2-3 claims your topic's conclusions rest on (the ones that, if wrong, change the product decision).

You are an ADVERSARIAL fact-checker. A researcher investigating "selling" for the Edinburgh Fringe ticketing landscape rests their conclusions on the claims below. Your job is to try to REFUTE each claim with your own independent web searches - do not reuse the researcher's sources as confirmation; find your own. A claim is "confirmed" only if independent evidence supports it; "plausible" if consistent with what you found but not independently confirmed; "refuted" if you found contrary evidence (then write the correction); "unverifiable" if the public record genuinely doesn't settle it. Be especially suspicious of: ownership claims (who runs/owns a website), "no such scheme exists" negatives (search for the scheme yourself before agreeing), and platform/vendor claims (which ticketing tech powers which site).

CLAIMS:
1. Neither the Edinburgh Festival Fringe Society nor any major venue operator offers an open affiliate, agent, white-label, or public purchase API; the only sanctioned data channel (Edinburgh Festivals Listings API) is listings-only and its licence forbids linking Fringe shows to any ticketing site other than edfringe.com.
2. Third-party selling of Fringe inventory is technically possible only through per-operator commercial agreements on the operators' own platforms (e.g. Spektrix's Agency API via a credit agreement the venue sets up; Red61 VIA API/white-label under contract) — there is no self-service route, no published commission rates, and the Fringe Society's own platform (Tikketr/equ) exposes no partner API at all.
3. The large venue operators have channelled cross-venue selling into their own closed joint venture EdFest.com (Red61-based, 7 operators, zero-commission/Love the Fringe model), and Fringe Society ticket T&Cs prohibit using tickets for 'commercial, business or re-sale purposes' — so for a small independent site the realistic option is uncommissioned deep links to edfringe.com and venue box offices, not selling.

## Ticketing Links Requirements

All links to individual Fringe shows or events must deep link to the appropriate URL on the edfringe.com website, for example https://www.edfringe.com/whats-on/childrens-shows/revolting-rhymes. Additionally, links relating to Fringe shows or events must not be made to any other ticketing site, including the venue's own site.

## Terms and Conditions for API Users

Users who publish work derived from the listings data must attribute it to the Edinburgh Festivals Listings API, for example by stating "data provided courtesy of the Edinburgh Festivals Listings API" or similar.

Any client applications must, wherever practical, attempt to retrieve fresh listings data if they have been offline for periods of longer than 24 hours.

Users must not redistribute listings to third parties by means of either data feeds or data dumps.

## Additional Requirements

If the API provider believes that use of the listings data is offensive, misleading or inaccurately represents the data in any way, they may request that users amend or remove any published material derived from the listings data.

Access to Edinburgh Festival Fringe listings is subject to approval.

I found comprehensive documentation about the Spektrix Agency API and credit agreements for third-party ticket agents. Here's what the search results show:

## Agency API Overview

The Agency API is specifically for access by third party agents who will be buying tickets from the system owner through a credit agreement. The Agency API allows Spektrix clients to give Agents live access to sell for events.

## Credit Agreement Framework

When an Agent processes a sale, the payment registers as Agent Credit payment / refund type, which can be found in the Credit, deposit & vouchers tab in the payment section of the Cart/Basket. You will not directly receive the payment when a transaction is made through the API. Instead, payments made through the API will go directly to the Agent. To collect the payment, you will need to invoice the Agent.

## Agent Setup and Commission Structures

The Client will set up a Customer record that acts as an Agent, which provides access credentials for Agents. As an Agent you can be set up with multiple customer records, each with different sales commission agreements, seat access and discounting where necessary.

A commission structure allows you to add a commission rate inside the ticket price, which is the value that is retained by the Agent.

The documentation is available on Spektrix's official support center and integration portal (integrate.spektrix.com).

You are researching for EdFringeNow, a client-side web product for the Edinburgh Festival Fringe (discovery + trip planner). The repo currently gets its show catalogue by scraping edfringe.com's GraphQL API (Tikketr platform, edfringe-tikketr-web-api.equhost.com) nightly via GitHub Actions. The owner wants to understand how Fringe tickets are ACTUALLY sold, who all the "event providers" (venue operators) are, whether a third party can sell tickets itself (affiliate/agent/API), and whether provider or aggregator listings APIs could replace the edfringe scrape.

TODAY is 2026-07-31. The 2026 Fringe runs 7-31 August (3,649 shows, 258 venues). Prefer 2025/2026 sources; older sources are fine for structural facts if you say so.

TOOLING CONSTRAINTS: You have WebSearch and WebFetch. edfringe.com returns 403 to WebFetch and equhost.com is blocked by the egress proxy - for those domains rely on WebSearch result snippets and third-party coverage. Most other sites (venue operators, news, wikis) are fetchable; if a fetch fails, fall back to search. Cite EVERY fact with a real URL you actually saw.

OUTPUT: your final output is consumed by a script, not a human. Fill the schema honestly: mark confidence low when a claim rests on one thin source; put what you could NOT establish into openQuestions rather than guessing. keyClaims = the 2-3 claims your topic's conclusions rest on (the ones that, if wrong, change the product decision).

You are an ADVERSARIAL fact-checker. A researcher investigating "listings" for the Edinburgh Fringe ticketing landscape rests their conclusions on the claims below. Your job is to try to REFUTE each claim with your own independent web searches - do not reuse the researcher's sources as confirmation; find your own. A claim is "confirmed" only if independent evidence supports it; "plausible" if consistent with what you found but not independently confirmed; "refuted" if you found contrary evidence (then write the correction); "unverifiable" if the public record genuinely doesn't settle it. Be especially suspicious of: ownership claims (who runs/owns a website), "no such scheme exists" negatives (search for the scheme yourself before agreeing), and platform/vendor claims (which ticketing tech powers which site).

CLAIMS:
1. No public machine-readable source other than edfringe.com's own GraphQL exposes per-performance ticket-availability/sold-out status - the official Listings API, all venue-operator sites, and all aggregators lack it - so any availability feature requires continuing to hit edfringe.com in some form.
2. The official Edinburgh Festivals Listings API's fringe feed is the official registered-show catalogue (same universe as edfringe.com, 2026 data live, per-performance times/prices, near-real-time modified pipeline) and is the only licensed, free replacement for the catalogue scrape - but it is gated by an app-approval process and its licence forbids linking to any ticketing site other than edfringe.com.
3. No venue operator publishes a public listings API or feed (Assembly's Directus CMS is locked, Gilded Balloon's open wp-json has no show type, the rest are HTML-only/Wix/403), and no commercial aggregator offers usable full-programme Fringe coverage except Data Thistle, which is paid, contact-for-pricing.

Based on the web search results, here's information about the Edinburgh Festivals Listings API terms, conditions, and licence:

## Overview

The Edinburgh Festivals Listings API provides open access to the event listings of Edinburgh's 11 major Festivals. It is a free-to-use API with over 640,000 performances and growing, providing up-to-date listings data for applications or research projects.

## Terms and Conditions

The API is operated by Festivals Edinburgh Limited, a company registered in Scotland, and the terms and conditions permit users to use the Edinburgh Festivals Listings API. The agreement is formed when you register for access to the API and the registration is accepted, and by applying for access you agree to abide by the terms and conditions.

## Licence Requirements

Where you publish any work derived from the listings data, you must attribute it to the Edinburgh Festivals Listings API and include a reference to the API web page at https://api.edinburghfestivalcity.com/.

For Fringe-specific data, under the terms of the licence you must only use the links to edfringe.com provided by the API and must not link to any other ticketing site from any content provided through the API.

## Fringe Data Access

To access live Edinburgh Festival Fringe data you will need to apply for approval, and all users can access a set of randomised Fringe data for testing.

The full terms and conditions are available at https://api.edinburghfestivalcity.com/licence.

# Fringe Listings Data Access

**Approval Process:**
Yes, there is a mandatory approval process. Developers must "build their applications using a demonstration dataset and submit them for review" before accessing live Fringe data.

**Key Requirements:**

1. **Linking restrictions:** "You must only use the links to edfringe.com provided by the API and must not link to any other ticketing site (including the venue's own site) from any content provided through the API."

2. **Ticketing display:** Apps should "simply display the `price` and `concession` prices" and use the website parameter to direct users to the Fringe site for full ticketing details.

3. **Data currency:** Applications must "retrieve fresh data from the API at least every 24 hours" to maintain accuracy.

4. **Genre representation:** The Fringe "strongly encourage[s] apps to not cover individual genres alone," reflecting their commitment to equal representation.

5. **Submission requirements:** Applicants must provide email, phone number, app description, how data will be displayed, and relevant URLs or screenshots.

The approval process involves initial development approval, followed by building with demonstration data (`?festival=demofringe`), then final review before live access is granted.

The API comes with significant disclaimers: "We do not contract to make it available now or at any time or to provide any particular level of service and we reserve the right to suspend the availability of the API at any time." (Disclaimers section)

The provider excludes liability for inaccurate data and service failures.

verdicts.claim: Neither the Edinburgh Festival Fringe Society nor any major venue operator offers an open affiliate, agent, white-label, or public purchase API; the only sanctioned data channel (Edinburgh Festivals Listings API) is listings-only and its licence forbids linking Fringe shows to any ticketing site other than edfringe.com.
verdicts.why: The licence half is confirmed verbatim from the primary source: I fetched https://api.edinburghfestivalcity.com/licence directly; clause 13 requires Fringe links to 'deep link to the appropriate URL on the edfringe.com website' and states 'Links relating to Fringe shows or events must not be made to any other ticketing site, including the venue's own site', clauses 17/19/21.4 ban redistribution, and the licence contains no purchase/ticketing functionality — listings-only, with Fringe access subject to approval (https://api.edinburghfestivalcity.com/documentation/fringe_approval). The 'no open scheme' negative survived adversarial searching: dedicated searches for affiliate/agent/white-label programmes from the Fringe Society and from Underbelly/Pleasance/Assembly/Gilded Balloon returned nothing (only consumer offers like Gilded Balloon 'Postcode Pals', https://www.broadwayworld.com/scotland/article/Gilded-Balloon-to-Launch-Postcode-Pals-Offering-6-Edinburgh-Fringe-Tickets-20260715); the Fringe Society's own participant-facing ticketing page describes only the central box office model (25% minimum allocation, 5%+VAT commission) with no partner/agent programme (https://www.edfringe.com/take-part/artists/organise-a-show/ticketing/). Caveat: the negative rests on absence of evidence, but the licence's own link-restriction rules structurally corroborate it — an open affiliate scheme would contradict the Society's sole sanctioned data channel.

verdicts.claim: Third-party selling of Fringe inventory is technically possible only through per-operator commercial agreements on the operators' own platforms (e.g. Spektrix's Agency API via a credit agreement the venue sets up; Red61 VIA API/white-label under contract) — there is no self-service route, no published commission rates, and the Fringe Society's own platform (Tikketr/equ) exposes no partner API at all.
verdicts.why: Spektrix mechanics confirmed from primary docs I fetched directly: https://integrate.spektrix.com/docs/agentguide states the Spektrix client (venue) sets up the Agent customer record, agents buy 'through a credit agreement', commission is 'set up individually on each Agent Customer account' — explicitly no self-service signup and no published rates; corroborated by https://support.spektrix.com/hc/en-us/articles/360030131111-Working-with-Agents-via-the-Agency-API. Red61 confirmed from its own site: it offers an API and a hosted white-label solution 'available to businesses when they partner with Red61' — contract-gated, no public pricing (https://www.red61.com/api-ticketing-integrations/, https://www.red61.com/wordpress-white-label-websites/); its one named aggregator integration, TickX, is a partner integration not self-service (https://www.tickx.com/technology-integrations/red61-partner-integration). On Tikketr/equ: searches for any Tikketr or equ developer/partner programme found nothing — equ's own case study (https://equ.com.au/work/edinburgh-fringe-festival/) describes a 'dedicated API' built for edfringe.com/the app (sign-ups, ticket purchasing) that is internal to the Fringe's own properties, with no public documentation or partner portal anywhere. Caveat: 'exposes no partner API at all' is a negative provable only by absence, but I could not find a trace of one; note the internal equ API does handle purchasing (it is what the repo scrapes), it is just not offered to partners.

verdicts.claim: The large venue operators have channelled cross-venue selling into their own closed joint venture EdFest.com (Red61-based, 7 operators, zero-commission/Love the Fringe model), and Fringe Society ticket T&Cs prohibit using tickets for 'commercial, business or re-sale purposes' — so for a small independent site the realistic option is uncommissioned deep links to edfringe.com and venue box offices, not selling.
verdicts.why: Independently confirmed on every component. Seven operators: an April 2026 article I fetched directly (https://www.beyondthejoke.co.uk/content/17535/love-fringe-tickets) names exactly seven — Assembly, C Arts, Gilded Balloon, Just the Tonic, Pleasance, Underbelly, Zoo — and quotes the commission-removal model ('By removing commission fees on ticket sales through the platform...'); edfest.com's own pages (via search snippets; direct fetch blocked with 503) describe 'a unique collaboration' of the same seven and state shows qualify for 0% EdFest commission if they allocate a minimum 4% of inventory to Love the Fringe (https://edfest.com/artists-producers, https://edfest.com/about). Red61-based: edfest.com/artists-producers tells companies to manage Love the Fringe allocations 'through their Red61 reporting site' and add/remove tickets 'through Red61'; Red61 is the Edinburgh firm that ran Fringe Society ticketing from 2002 (https://www.red61.com/news/red61-celebrates-20-years-at-the-edinburgh-festival-fringe/). T&Cs: edfringe.com's terms page states 'you agree not to use tickets for any commercial, business or re-sale purposes' (https://www.edfringe.com/legal-information/terms-and-conditions/, via search snippet since edfringe.com 403s direct fetches). The 'uncommissioned deep links' conclusion follows: the Listings API licence mandates deep links to edfringe.com and no affiliate/commission scheme exists per claim 1. Minor residual ambiguity, not decision-changing: one search summary suggested some EdFest pages may say 'eight' venues or mention theSpaceUK, but both the site-restricted search of edfest.com and the April 2026 launch coverage give the same seven, without theSpaceUK.

## Spektrix API v3 Instances Status Endpoint

The `/instances/{{instanceID}}/status` endpoint is accessed via a GET call to return a summary of availability for the specified Event Instance. The endpoint URL is: `https://system.spektrix.com/{{clientname}}/api/v3/instances/{{instanceID}}/status`

### Parameters and Features

The endpoint includes an `includeChildPlans=true` parameter that can be used to retrieve additional information.

An extended detail version is available at `/instances/{{id}}/status/detail` with parameters like `includeLockInformation=true` and `includeChildPlans=true`.

### Authentication and Availability

Seat availability will differ based upon the authenticated customer account (or lack thereof) if locks with customer eligibility have been assigned to any seats in the Instance's seating plan.

### General API Documentation

A full list of all available endpoints can be found at `https://system.spektrix.com/apitesting/api/v3/Help`, which provides information on available endpoints, request parameters, and response examples.

The search results indicate this endpoint is documented on the integrate.spektrix.com platform and is part of the standard Spektrix API v3 integration documentation.

verdicts.claim: No public machine-readable source other than edfringe.com's own GraphQL exposes per-performance ticket-availability/sold-out status - the official Listings API, all venue-operator sites, and all aggregators lack it - so any availability feature requires continuing to hit edfringe.com in some form.
verdicts.correction: Nearly true but false as stated. The official Listings API does lack availability (verified: its events schema has per-performance start/end/price/concession but no availability or sold-out field, only event-level cancelled/deleted status and static performance_space capacity). However, at least one Fringe venue operator publicly exposes per-performance availability in machine-readable form: Traverse Theatre (whose TravFest26 is its Edinburgh Fringe 2026 season, venue page on edfringe.com) runs a fully public, unauthenticated Spektrix v3 JSON API. I fetched https://system.spektrix.com/traverse/api/v3/events (1,039 events, 15 in Aug 2026 incl. Bog Witch, Cathy, For Dolores, Little Animals) and https://system.spektrix.com/traverse/api/v3/instances/331402AKLVTMQPNDQGHRRJGSHCTCVJQTP/status?includeChildPlans=true, which returned live seat counts {"available":19,"capacity":302,"unavailable":283} for the 2 Aug 2026 Bog Witch performance. Capital Theatres' Spektrix API (client 'capitaltheatres') is also openly readable. So the corrected statement is: full-programme availability requires edfringe.com (no operator- or aggregator-level source covers more than its own handful of shows, and the big operators - Assembly, Underbelly, Gilded Balloon, Pleasance - surface sold-out only inside rendered HTML), but 'no public machine-readable source' is wrong: Spektrix-based venue box offices expose it per performance, publicly, today. Note also that venue-box-office availability reflects the venue's own allocation, which can differ from edfringe.com's sold-out state.
verdicts.why: I independently verified the Listings API's lack of availability fields from its own events documentation (https://api.edinburghfestivalcity.com/documentation/events: performances have id/type/price/concession/price_string/start/end/duration_minutes; no availability field; capacity only under performance_space). I then found the counterexample myself: traverse.co.uk embeds Spektrix web components with client-name="traverse"; live unauthenticated GETs to https://system.spektrix.com/traverse/api/v3/events and the per-instance /status endpoint (documented at https://integrate.spektrix.com/docs/Availability, 'a summary of availability for the specified Event Instance') returned real seat-availability numbers for a Fringe 2026 performance. TravFest26 being the Traverse's Edinburgh Fringe season is confirmed by https://www.whatsonstage.com/news/traverse-theatre-announces-2026-edinburgh-fringe-season_1721136/ and https://www.traverse.co.uk/news/travfest26-a-bold-august-programme-of-new-writing-from-scotland-and-beyond, and https://www.edfringe.com/tickets/venues/traverse-theatre appears as the Fringe venue page in search results. For the big operators I checked myself: Underbelly event pages (e.g. https://www.underbellyedinburgh.co.uk/events/event/afronauts) show a 'Sold out / Unavailable' calendar legend but only as server-rendered HTML (jQuery/Alpine site, no JSON endpoint found in app.min.js); Assembly's whats-on is a Nuxt SSR app whose visible /api routes are basket/user/adverts only; The Stand's JSON-LD Event markup has no offers/availability.

verdicts.claim: The official Edinburgh Festivals Listings API's fringe feed is the official registered-show catalogue (same universe as edfringe.com, 2026 data live, per-performance times/prices, near-real-time modified pipeline) and is the only licensed, free replacement for the catalogue scrape - but it is gated by an app-approval process and its licence forbids linking to any ticketing site other than edfringe.com.
verdicts.why: Every load-bearing part verified against the primary source, independently fetched. Official + free: the documentation page states verbatim 'We offer a free-to-use API to the official event listings database for Edinburgh's 11 major Festivals' (https://api.edinburghfestivalcity.com/documentation), operated by Festivals Edinburgh Limited (SC331673, https://api.edinburghfestivalcity.com/). 2026 data live: the status page (https://api.edinburghfestivalcity.com/status) marks Edinburgh Festival Fringe 2026 as available, with access 'subject to approval'. Per-performance times/prices: the events schema (https://api.edinburghfestivalcity.com/documentation/events) documents a performances array with start, end, duration_minutes, price, concession, price_string. Modified pipeline: https://api.edinburghfestivalcity.com/documentation/querying documents the modified_from parameter with guidance to poll using a timestamp ten minutes before the last request, and requires re-sync at least every 24 hours. App-approval gate: https://api.edinburghfestivalcity.com/documentation/fringe_approval requires building against the demofringe dataset and submitting the app for review before live Fringe access. Linking ban: same page and licence Section 13 (https://api.edinburghfestivalcity.com/licence): links to Fringe shows 'must not be made to any other ticketing site, including the venue's own site' and must deep-link to edfringe.com - which also entails the feed shares edfringe.com's show universe (it supplies edfringe.com URLs per show). Two qualifiers are plausible rather than proven: 'near-real-time' upstream latency is not documented (the status page admits 'a short delay' between programme launch and API appearance), and 'only licensed free replacement' is a negative - I found no other free licensed full-catalogue source (Data Thistle is licensed but paid), but cannot prove exhaustiveness.

verdicts.claim: No venue operator publishes a public listings API or feed (Assembly's Directus CMS is locked, Gilded Balloon's open wp-json has no show type, the rest are HTML-only/Wix/403), and no commercial aggregator offers usable full-programme Fringe coverage except Data Thistle, which is paid, contact-for-pricing.
verdicts.correction: The headline negative is false: at least two Fringe venue operators publish public machine-readable listings feeds. (1) Traverse Theatre: fully public unauthenticated Spektrix v3 JSON API at https://system.spektrix.com/traverse/api/v3/events (its complete Fringe 2026 TravFest programme with descriptions, dates, isOnSale, images) plus per-instance availability endpoints. (2) Summerhall Arts: its festival site festival.summerhallarts.co.uk has an open WordPress REST API with dedicated 'events' and 'performances' custom post types - https://festival.summerhallarts.co.uk/wp-json/wp/v2/events and .../performances return Fringe 2026 shows (e.g. 'Adam Riches: The Captain', 'QFWFQ') with dates, venues and genres taxonomies; the researcher likely tested only summerhall.co.uk, which does return 403. The individually checkable details mostly hold: Gilded Balloon's wp-json exposes no show type (verified: types are post/page/attachment/jobs/venues/home-page-post etc.), Monkey Barrel is Wix, Underbelly is server-rendered HTML with no JSON API found, Summerhall's main domain 403s, and Data Thistle is paid contact-for-pricing with full Fringe coverage. The Assembly-Directus detail is unverifiable (Nuxt SSR app; no Directus evidence either way; cms./directus./api. subdomains unresolvable). The aggregator part stands as stated.
verdicts.why: All from my own fetches on 2026-07-31: https://system.spektrix.com/traverse/api/v3/events returned 1,039 events as JSON with no auth, 15 dated August 2026 matching Traverse's announced Fringe season (cross-checked via https://www.whatsonstage.com/news/traverse-theatre-announces-2026-edinburgh-fringe-season_1721136/). https://festival.summerhallarts.co.uk/wp-json/wp/v2/types lists events/performances/venues/archived-events post types and .../wp-json/wp/v2/events?per_page=2 and .../performances?per_page=2 both returned HTTP 200 with Fringe 2026 show records. https://gildedballoon.co.uk/wp-json/wp/v2/types confirmed no show/event type. https://www.monkeybarrelcomedy.com is Wix (1,700+ wix asset references). https://www.summerhall.co.uk returned HTTP 403 to my fetch. Data Thistle: https://www.datathistle.com/ offers an Events API (api.datathistle.com) in JSON/XML/CSV with no published pricing - 'request a demo' / 'Get in touch' model - and https://edinburghfestival.datathistle.com/festival/edinburgh-festival-fringe/ shows full Fringe 2026 festival coverage. I found no other commercial aggregator with full-programme coverage (searches surfaced only the official Listings API and Data Thistle), though that negative cannot be proven exhaustively.

content.content:
SUMMARY:
 Nothing publicly available can fully replace the edfringe.com GraphQL scrape, because no other machine-readable source exposes per-performance ticket availability; but the official Edinburgh Festivals Listings API (api.edinburghfestivalcity.com, operated by Festivals Edinburgh Ltd, managed by inGenerator) is a viable licensed backbone for the catalogue itself. Its Fringe feed is the official registered-show database (the same universe as edfringe.com's ~3,649 registered shows, including Laughing Horse Free Festival shows, which must register, and most PBH Free Fringe shows, for which registration is optional), with per-performance start/end/price, cancelled/deleted status, a near-real-time last_modified sync pipeline ("a delay of a few minutes"), a 24h minimum refresh rule, 2026 data live in its explorer, and even a beta MCP endpoint - but no sold-out/availability field, a mandatory app-approval process using a demofringe dummy dataset, and a hard licence rule that you may only link to edfringe.com URLs supplied by the API (never venue or other ticketing sites). Its projects page shows it actively approves discovery/planner apps nearly identical to EdFringeNow (Fringe Vibes, FringeFlow, TicketBadger, Plan My Fringe). Direct probing of all seven major venue-operator sites found no public machine-readable listings anywhere: Assembly runs a Nuxt front-end fed by a locked Directus CMS (assemblyfestival.pazaz.studio returns 403 anonymously) that syncs from Red61 ticketing; Gilded Balloon's open wp-json exposes no show/event post type; Pleasance (Drupal), Underbelly and The Stand render listings only as server-side HTML with no JSON-LD; Monkey Barrel is a Wix site; Summerhall 403s non-browser clients; no iCal/ics feeds exist on any of them. Among aggregators, Data Thistle (The List's data arm) is the only one with real festival coverage - it explicitly sells "Edinburgh Festival" events data via a commercial API with no published pricing - while Skiddle's API is beta and non-commercial-only with thin Fringe coverage, Eventbrite carries only stray unregistered free-comedy events, WeGotTickets' Edinburgh region search shows zero Fringe listings, and Ents24's authenticated API has unverified (likely minimal) Fringe coverage. Bottom line ranking: (1) official Listings API for the full catalogue (free, licensed, stable, but availability-blind and approval-gated); (2) continued edfringe GraphQL scraping, reduced to an availability/sold-out overlay if the API is adopted; (3) Data Thistle only if paying for a commercial licence makes sense; (4) per-venue feeds and other aggregators are not viable at all. The practical combination is official API catalogue + a slimmed edfringe availability probe, noting the unresolved licence question of blending scraped availability with API data.

VERDICTS:
--- REFUTED
CLAIM: No public machine-readable source other than edfringe.com's own GraphQL exposes per-performance ticket-availability/sold-out status - the official Listings API, all venue-operator sites, and all aggregators lack it - so any availability feature requires continuing to hit edfringe.com in some form.
WHY: I independently verified the Listings API's lack of availability fields from its own events documentation (https://api.edinburghfestivalcity.com/documentation/events: performances have id/type/price/concession/price_string/start/end/duration_minutes; no availability field; capacity only under performance_space). I then found the counterexample myself: traverse.co.uk embeds Spektrix web components with client-name="traverse"; live unauthenticated GETs to https://system.spektrix.com/traverse/api/v3/events and the per-instance /status endpoint (documented at https://integrate.spektrix.com/docs/Availability, 'a summary of availability for the specified Event Instance') returned real seat-availability numbers for a Fringe 2026 performance. TravFest26 being the Traverse's Edinburgh Fringe season is confirmed by https://www.whatsonstage.com/news/traverse-theatre-announces-2026-edinburgh-fringe-season_1721136/ and https://www.traverse.co.uk/news/travfest26-a-bold-august-programme-of-new-writing-from-scotland-and-beyond, and https://www.edfringe.com/tickets/venues/traverse-theatre appears as the Fringe venue page in search results. For the big operators I checked myself: Underbelly event pages (e.g. https://www.underbellyedinburgh.co.uk/events/event/afronauts) show a 'Sold out / Unavailable' calendar legend but only as server-rendered HTML (jQuery/Alpine site, no JSON endpoint found in app.min.js); Assembly's whats-on is a Nuxt SSR app whose visible /api routes are basket/user/adverts
CORRECTION: Nearly true but false as stated. The official Listings API does lack availability (verified: its events schema has per-performance start/end/price/concession but no availability or sold-out field, only event-level cancelled/deleted status and static performance_space capacity). However, at least one Fringe venue operator publicly exposes per-performance availability in machine-readable form: Traverse Theatre (whose TravFest26 is its Edinburgh Fringe 2026 season, venue page on edfringe.com) runs a fully public, unauthenticated Spektrix v3 JSON API. I fetched https://system.spektrix.com/traverse/api/v3/events (1,039 events, 15 in Aug 2026 incl. Bog Witch, Cathy, For Dolores, Little Animals) and https://system.spektrix.com/traverse/api/v3/instances/331402AKLVTMQPNDQGHRRJGSHCTCVJQTP/status?includeChildPlans=true, which returned live seat counts {"available":19,"capacity":302,"unavailable":283} for the 2 Aug 2026 Bog Witch performance. Capital Theatres' Spektrix API (client 'capitaltheatres') is also openly readable. So the corrected statement is: full-programme availability requires edfringe.com (no operator- or aggregator-level source covers more than its own handful of shows, and the big operators - Assembly, Underbelly, Gilded Balloon, Pleasance - surface sold-out only inside rendered HTML), but 'no public machine-readable source' is wrong: Spektrix-based venue box offices expose it per performance, publicly, today. Note also that venue-box-office availability reflects the venue's own allocation, which can differ from edfringe.com's sold-out state.
--- CONFIRMED
CLAIM: The official Edinburgh Festivals Listings API's fringe feed is the official registered-show catalogue (same universe as edfringe.com, 2026 data live, per-performance times/prices, near-real-time modified pipeline) and is the only licensed, free replacement for the catalogue scrape - but it is gated by an app-approval process and its licence forbids linking to any ticketing site other than edfringe.com.
WHY: Every load-bearing part verified against the primary source, independently fetched. Official + free: the documentation page states verbatim 'We offer a free-to-use API to the official event listings database for Edinburgh's 11 major Festivals' (https://api.edinburghfestivalcity.com/documentation), operated by Festivals Edinburgh Limited (SC331673, https://api.edinburghfestivalcity.com/). 2026 data live: the status page (https://api.edinburghfestivalcity.com/status) marks Edinburgh Festival Fringe 2026 as available, with access 'subject to approval'. Per-performance times/prices: the events schema (https://api.edinburghfestivalcity.com/documentation/events) documents a performances array with start, end, duration_minutes, price, concession, price_string. Modified pipeline: https://api.edinburghfestivalcity.com/documentation/querying documents the modified_from parameter with guidance to poll using a timestamp ten minutes before the last request, and requires re-sync at least every 24 hours. App-approval gate: https://api.edinburghfestivalcity.com/documentation/fringe_approval requires building against the demofringe dataset and submitting the app for review before live Fringe access. Linking ban: same page and licence Section 13 (https://api.edinburghfestivalcity.com/licence): links to Fringe shows 'must not be made to any other ticketing site, including the venue's own site' and must deep-link to edfringe.com - which also entails the feed shares edfringe.com's show universe (

content.content:
######################### operators
The dominant structural fact: almost every major commercial Fringe venue operator runs its own online box office in parallel with edfringe.com, and 10 of the 15 operators investigated run it on the same platform — Red61's VIA system — usually as a white-label WordPress front end hosted at *.online.red61.co.uk with VIA composite event IDs (e.g. Underbelly event=61:9440, Gilded Balloon /event/14:6104, ZOO 124:1938, C ARTS 34:3397, theSpaceUK 911:3690, Pleasance /via/tickets/33:301593). Confirmed Red61 sellers: Assembly, Pleasance, Underbelly, Gilded Balloon, Summerhall, ZOO, C ARTS, theSpaceUK, Just the Tonic, and Scottish Storytelling Centre; the exceptions are Traverse (Spektrix), The Stand (own in-house system at thestand.co.uk), Monkey Barrel (Line-Up/liveit.io for its own sales, with Fringe runs pushed to edfringe), Greenside (no own online ticketing found — effectively edfringe-only), and Dance Base (sells through Assembly's Red61 channel under a 2026 partnership). Parallel selling is structural and rule-based: every Fringe show must allocate a minimum of 25% of tickets per performance to the Fringe Box Office (sliding scale above that), with 5%+VAT commission to the Fringe Society; Summerhall's published 2025 information pack states that typically 70% of its tickets sell through the EdFringe Box Office and 30% through its own box office, whose system is "linked to the Fringe box office". Venue box offices also cross-sell each other's shows — C ARTS names Assembly, Gilded Balloon, Just the Tonic, Paradise Green, Pleasance, Summerhall, Underbelly and Zoo as cross-selling partners, and Red61 describes 17 interconnected Fringe instances in 2024 — and venues actively incentivise direct booking (Gilded Balloon: "exclusive discounts and low booking fees when booking direct"). The "Big Four" (Assembly, Gilded Balloon, Pleasance, Underbelly) briefly jointly marketed as the "Edinburgh Comedy Festival" in 2008-09 before the brand was dropped; the grouping survives only as an informal label, with William Burdett-Coutts still Assembly's artistic director. Edinburgh Playhouse in 2026 is both an ATG receiving house and a registered Fringe venue (venue number 59) hosting a handful of big ATG-ticketed comedy one-nighters (Daniel Sloss, Troy Hawke, Connor Burns, Michelle Wolf) that are also listed on edfringe.com. Implication for EdFringeNow: edfringe.com remains the only single catalogue covering all operators, but the venue-side ecosystem is essentially one platform (Red61 VIA) plus Spektrix/Line-Up/in-house outliers, so any provider-API strategy is really a question about Red61 access.

######################### free-tail
The two big free-show operators work differently. PBH's Free Fringe (founded 1996) is strictly unticketed: entry is free, there are no advance tickets or reservations, and audiences drop voluntary donations in a bucket; its listings live on freefringe.org.uk, in apps, and in the printed Wee Blue Book, with ~50+ venue spaces and roughly 800 listing entries for 2026 — and crucially, Fringe Society registration is OPTIONAL for PBH acts ("It's not compulsory to be in the program"), so only 183 PBH shows appear in the edfringe 2026 catalogue. Laughing Horse's Free Festival (freefestival.co.uk) is mostly free-unticketed with donations, but also offers Pay What You Can advance reservations sold through the official Fringe Box Office (not Eventbrite); in the 2026 scrape its 320 shows split into 103 FREE_NON_TICKETED and 215 plain TICKETS_AVAILABLE (the PWYC ones). Mid-tier independents confirmed active in 2025/2026 include Paradise Green (2 venues/5 spaces), Bedlam Theatre (EUTC), Braw Venues @ Hill Street (+ Grand Lodge), Greenside @ Riddles Court, the Institut français d'Écosse ("Vive le Fringe!"), and the Quaker Meeting House now programmed by C ARTS as "C alto"; Sweet Venues has left Edinburgh (Brighton/Dundee only) and Army @ The Fringe is absent from the 2026 catalogue. On completeness: the Fringe is open-access/unjuried — anyone may participate, but being "in the Fringe" requires paid show registration with the Fringe Society, and venues register (free) to appear in the published venue directory (tickets.edfringe.com/venues; the API's VenueTypeAhead yields 301 venue records for 2026) — so the edfringe catalogue is by construction the exhaustive universe of REGISTERED shows and venues, with the PBH unregistered-show long tail as the one demonstrable gap. The Association of Independent Venue Producers (fringealliance.org) exists on paper but its site is a dormant template, so the Fringe Society's own directory is the only practical enumeration source. Free shows do appear in edfringe data like any other show: the scrape's ticketStatus enum includes FREE_NON_TICKETED (399 shows) and FREE_TICKETED (23 shows), and every PBH-registered show carries FREE_NON_TICKETED — meaning the current scrape already covers the entire sellable and registered-free universe, and no free-show operator offers any third-party ticket-selling opportunity.

######################### selling
No open route exists for a third party to sell Edinburgh Fringe tickets. The Fringe Society offers no affiliate scheme, agent programme, white-label box office, or public purchase API; it is itself the central agent (every ticketed show must allocate >=25% of tickets to the Fringe Box Office, on which the Society takes 5%+VAT commission), its ticket T&Cs bar use of tickets "for any commercial, business or re-sale purposes", and its only sanctioned data channel — the free Edinburgh Festivals Listings API (api.edinburghfestivalcity.com, Fringe access subject to approval) — is listings-only and its licence explicitly forbids linking Fringe shows "to any other ticketing site, including the venue's own site" (edfringe.com links only). None of the big venue operators advertises an affiliate/agent programme either; instead seven of them (Assembly, C ARTS, Gilded Balloon, Just the Tonic, Pleasance, Underbelly, ZOO) run their own closed cross-venue storefront, EdFest.com (Red61-based, single basket, £5 fee cap, "zero commission" tied to their Love the Fringe membership). At the platform layer the technology for third-party selling does exist — Spektrix has a dedicated Agency API for agents buying on credit agreements, and Red61 VIA (which runs Gilded Balloon, ZOO, EdFest and ran the Society box office 2009-2023) offers APIs, white-label sales and venue cross-selling — but in every case access is granted per-client by the venue/operator under a negotiated commercial agreement; there is no self-service signup and no published commission rates. The Society's current platform (Tikketr, built by equ/Equilibrium Interactive) has no public partner API at all. Existing "third-party" sellers confirm the pattern: TodayTix and Fever carry no actual Edinburgh Fringe inventory (only London transfers/previews), LivingSocial merely retails Love the Fringe memberships as vouchers, and See Tickets/Ents24 retail The Stand's club shows only under explicit agency arrangements with that venue. Bottom line for a small independent site: "selling tickets ourselves" would mean negotiating separate agent/credit agreements with each of dozens of venue operators across at least five different ticketing platforms, with no published programme to apply to; the realistic approach is deep-linking to each seller (edfringe.com and/or venue box offices), accepting that no affiliate commission scheme currently exists anywhere in the Fringe ecosystem — deep links earn nothing, and the one licensed listings feed would additionally require linking only to edfringe.com.
